# B13 mip liveness and the A6 copy-primitive check

**Source result:** retain Complementary's composite6 RT3 mip request. Its
generated physical chain can reach the final pass after a second flip. A
narrow BSL candidate suppresses **only composite7's RT1 mip request**; the
complete downstream source uses explicit LOD0 and the original end-of-frame
filter reset closes the chain's sampling lifetime. BSL composite6 stays native.
Eight focused source/packaging tests pass. No candidate driver rendering,
physical-call deletion, pixel/lifecycle parity or speed is accepted.

This bounded B13 audit does not close the all-36 goal or other families. It
does not reopen A2's completed no-gain coupled cost screen. A6's existing private
`a0dab58d…f8ee80f3` remains unaccepted; the cheap check below is an additional
falsifier, not promotion.

## Provenance and private scope

records exact members/lines and original archive/source hashes. Extracted source
under that same ignored `mips/sources/` directory retains original bytes. The
complete original BSL shader/property digest is
`198235a39479dee0964f272104844ff2ee32fd4438309a54d1421278986066bb`.

The [builder](../../scripts/build_mip_liveness_candidate.py),
[manifest](../../patches/resource-experiments/mip-liveness-r1.json), and
[tests](../../tests/test_mip_liveness_candidate.py) are private and absent from
the production catalog. Candidate and native [receipts](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/BSL-MipLiveness-Candidate-r1.json)
are adjacent to their ignored ZIPs. Exactly one member changes:
`shaders/program/composite7.glsl`. The patch changes the directive to false only
for an activated private build with defined exact Iris/MC macros, `OVERWORLD`,
native TAA and LIGHT_SHAFT, and no RETRO_FILTER. Other branches retain true or
the native outer absence. It adds no option, target, pass, copy or uniform.
Properties, all other members and the BSL attribution header remain unchanged.
The original BSL release contains no separate license file; no distribution
authorization is inferred.

Private construction requires the exact JAR and **all 384 observed string
values**, including their full map digest, not only the relevant six toggles.
Observed SHADOW/LIGHT_SHAFT/FXAA/TAA are true, TAA_MODE is 0, RETRO_FILTER false.
The archive cannot hash the installed runtime. Root must rehash the loaded
archive/JAR and reobserve the complete map before use. BSL's `dimension.world0`
also contains `*`; root must verify actual `minecraft:overworld`, not infer it
from the wrapper. Other loader/version/dimension/private-map scopes are
uncertified. Source checks cover DH/PBR branches; actual DH/PBR remains pending.
Faithful product Off still selects the original archive.

## Complementary: the later physical consumer prevents suppression

Retained Reimagined [native 398 map](../../dev/logs/complementary-shadow-sequence-r11/expected-options.json)
has FXAA_DEFINE 1, FXAA_STRENGTH 75, TAA_DEFINE -1, IMAGE_SHARPENING 5,
UNDERWATER_DISTORTION true, WATER_REFRACTION_INTENSITY 2.0 and CHROMA_ABERRATION 0.
The native properties therefore keep composite7. TAA_DEFINE -1 is interpreted
by the native Iris branch in common.glsl; it is not a request to turn AA off.

Let P be RT3's physical current image after composite5 and Q the other image.
Names are symbolic; actual texture IDs/format/state are runtime observations.

| Order | Read / mip state | Physical write / later use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| composite5 | Bloom is read from the prior RT3 current image | Writes the final pre-TAA image to P at level0 |
| composite6 setup | Generates P mips and sets **P** min filter to LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR | No target content flip occurs in this setup |
| composite6 draw | `texelFetch(colortex3,…,0)` at program line33; TAA neighborhood line127 also LOD0 | Writes Q level0 via DRAWBUFFERS32, logical current becomes Q |
| composite7 draw | Q level0 `texelFetch`, plus FXAA implicit `texture2D` calls | Writes **P level0**, current becomes P; generated P higher levels are not overwritten by this level0 draw |
| final draw | **P** implicit `texture2D` base/sharpen/chroma/underwater path | Can observe the surviving P chain under its mip filter |
| final return / next frame | Iris resets minification on both RT3 storages | Reset ends this frame's mip-filter sampling lifetime; clearing level0 does not itself remove old higher levels |

Exact downstream sources:
[composite6](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/sources/complementary-reimagined/shaders/program/composite6.glsl:16),
[TAA](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/sources/complementary-reimagined/shaders/lib/antialiasing/taa.glsl:127),
[composite7](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/sources/complementary-reimagined/shaders/program/composite7.glsl:29),
[FXAA](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/sources/complementary-reimagined/shaders/lib/antialiasing/fxaa.glsl:89),
[final](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/sources/complementary-reimagined/shaders/program/final.glsl:93).
The FXAA implicit calls read Q, whose filter remains native LINEAR in this
chain; they are not themselves proof of P-mip use. The subsequent write to P
and final's implicit sampling are the decisive connection.

Underwater final coordinates add a sine displacement. With retained amplitude
`2.0 * 0.00035` and spatial frequency 25, its coordinate Jacobian can enlarge
a pixel footprint; implicit LOD is therefore not identically zero. Sharpener
offsets retain that coordinate derivative. This is a **source-visible live
consumer**, not proof that a retained dry still sampled a nonzero mip. Even if
the current dry image appeared equal, suppressing the chain would alter the
native supported underwater path. Explicit chroma is inactive in this map;
its nonzero settings would need the same filter analysis. The commented-out
box filter in final is not executable evidence.

Whole-archive references distinguish earlier custom cloud-water texture bindings
(`texture.deferred.colortex3`) from composite RT3. Earlier translucency,
bloom and cloud consumers precede this generation. No later composite8 or
composite6/7 compute companion intervenes. RT3 is RGBA8 and cleared; there are
no native explicit flip/scale overrides in these pins. These facts do not erase
the P chain's final use. R/U share these relevant member bytes; Unbound's own
effective map and runtime are unobserved, so no U activation claim follows.
Both retain the native request. Other Complementary requests are outside this
single-chain suppression contract.

## BSL: complete c7 last-use certificate

The selected request is
[composite7 line46](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/sources/bsl/shaders/program/composite7.glsl:46).
It is LIGHT_SHAFT-gated, while native properties enable the pass with
`TAA && !RETRO_FILTER`. The retained map activates both. SHADOW's native
settings gate can undefine LIGHT_SHAFT and is preserved. The direct includes
are settings and TAA; the whole pinned archive has no c7 compute companion,
later composite8, RT1 image alias, custom RT1 texture override, explicit flip,
or scale directive. The legacy alias `gdepth` adds no hidden post-c7 consumer.

Let P contain composite5 color, Q its counterpart; retained FXAA is enabled.

| Order | Original | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| composite6 | Generate P mip chain; read explicit0; write Q level0 | Unchanged, including its request and FXAA |
| composite7 setup | Generate **Q** chain and set Q min filter to mip-linear | Only this generation/filter switch absent |
| composite7/TAA | Read Q at explicit LOD0; write P level0 and RT2 history | Same programs, passes, flips, targets and arithmetic; Q uses native LINEAR filter |
| final | Read **P** at explicit LOD0, including sharpener/chroma/retro code | Identical source and physical bindings; P mip/filter state is unchanged |
| final reset | Both P/Q min filters restored to LINEAR | Same reset; extra old Q mip allocations may remain, but are not read |
| next-frame earlier consumers | Native LINEAR RT1 sampling after reset; default clear applies to both images | Same level0 initialization/filter contract; c6 regenerates its selected input before using any mip filter |

There are **12 direct RT1 read sites** after the request:
one composite7 initial sample; four TAA blur taps and one neighborhood-clipping
site; final base plus sharpener plus four chroma sites. Every one is
`texture2DLod(colortex1,…,0)` or `0.0`. The generic Catmull-Rom helper is called
with **colortex2**, not RT1; selective-TAA mask is RT3; DH/VOXY branches change
depth/reprojection inputs, not current-color LOD. Final's sharpener, chroma and
retro-coordinate variants still select explicit LOD0. The saved whole-archive
inventory plus exact source digest bounds the consumer search.

This removes generation work, not allocation or a graphics pass. It does not
change native AA, light shafts, exposure, bloom, PBR or DH arithmetic. BSL c6's
request is a separate possible opportunity and deliberately remains unchanged.
No broad all-BSL/all-options runtime support is claimed by the narrow private
map. The [source tests](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/tests-first.txt)
pass eight tests, including 24 original/candidate dimension/stage/DH/PBR source
comparisons, missing/unknown macro fallback, native option fallback, complete
map rejection, mutated/new-consumer refusal, exact JAR/class pins, all member
preservation and deterministic artifacts. Clang preprocessing is not Iris
preprocessing or driver compilation.

Lead challenged whether the new conditional declaration would be scanned raw,
allowing a later native `true` branch to win. **Closed for the exact source
parser:** ShaderPack's constructor stores a sourceProvider whose `lambda$new$8`
expands includes and calls `JcppProcessor.glslPreprocessSource` before returning;
ProgramSet passes that returned fragment string to ProgramSource, whose
constructor then creates ProgramDirectives. Its false directive callback removes
the target from the mip set. The raw fallback declarations are therefore not
all scanned together. A separate [exact Iris/JCPP parser check](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/iris-directive-check/result-full.txt)
ran the pinned JAR's JcppProcessor and ConstDirectiveParser on the isolated guard
and expanded full world0 c7 source: six cases each produced exactly one mip
directive, false for the active candidate and true for native/unknown10813.
[Arguments/input/library hashes](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/iris-directive-check/receipt-full.json)
retain provenance. The first attempt's missing SLF4J dependency is preserved;
adding the local API JAR resolved that test setup failure. These are actual
offline Iris parser executions, not live renderer activation or driver tests.

## Exact Iris resource and filter basis

The reused [20-class bytecode receipt](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r1/pass-liveness/iris-bytecode-receipt.json)
pins the installed JAR. `CompositeRenderer.setupMipmapping(RenderTarget,boolean)`
selects main/alt from the pass's **stageReadsFromAlt**, calls
`IrisRenderSystem.generateMipmaps(texture, GL_TEXTURE_2D)`, then changes only
that texture's MIN_FILTER to 9987 (noninteger) or 9984 (integer).
`renderAll` does this before framebuffer bind and `Program.use`, not after the
pass draw. Constructor flips are already represented in each pass's snapshot.

`RenderTargets.createColorFramebuffer(readsFromAlt,drawBuffers)` writes the
**opposite** physical image for each target. `RenderTarget.getMainTexture()`,
`getAltTexture()`, `getInternalFormat()`, `getWidth()` and `getHeight()` are actual
public APIs; `RenderTargets.get(int)` is the lookup. The exact
[Pass fields](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/CompositeRenderer-Pass.fields.txt)
are `name`, `program`, `drawBuffers`, `framebuffer`, `stageReadsFromAlt`,
`mipmappedBuffers`, `viewWidth`, `viewHeight`, `viewportScale`,
`flippedAtLeastOnce`, `computes`, and `blendModeOverride`.

IrisSamplers registers RT1 and its alias with a **null GlSampler**. Exact
[SamplerBinding bytecode](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/ProgramSamplers-SamplerBinding.javap.txt)
maps null to sampler0 and binds it before binding the texture. Thus ordinary
texture state governs this native path. RenderTarget starts both noninteger
storages with MIN/MAG LINEAR and clamp-edge. Native RT1 format is declared RGB8
in BSL final, inside a directive comment; actual parsed/driver format must be
observed. PackRenderTargetDirectives defaults clear=true; BSL has no RT1 clear
override. ClearPassCreator clears both physical storages. FinalPassRenderer
resets both MIN filters after final rendering, before any final swap copies;
clear-listed targets are excluded from its swap-copy list.

Explicit LOD0 is bilinear level0 under either relevant min filter when actual
base level and LOD clamps are native. Root must still observe sampler binding0,
BASE_LEVEL0, MIN/MAX_LOD, format, level extents, unchanged storage lifetime and
absence of external overrides. Do not infer these from Java getters alone.
Old allocated Q mip bytes are allowed to differ. Resize/reload/aborted-frame
behavior and third-party GL state are runtime qualifications, not source wins.

**One next B13 test:** root performs a bounded untimed original/native/candidate/
return qualification on this exact BSL map. Join actual c7 source/program/pass
and RT1 input/output; observe original `mipmappedBuffers={1}`, candidate absence
of 1, and the actual selected generation call gone with c6 still present. Check
sampler/filter/base/LOD state and synchronized TAA/current/history/final outputs.
If activation, binding or equality fails, stop before cost. If it passes, a
bounded matched total-cost screen can decide usefulness; no synthetic mip-only
timing or source test establishes a rendering gain.

Sildur's pinned archive has no recognized `*MipmapEnabled` request to remove.
Its explicit LOD1 VL/godray reads do not establish Iris generation or a dead
chain. This closes this narrow request search only. Photon, MakeUp, Solas,
Bliss, AstraLex and other chains remain unknown for B13.

## A6: cheap same-frame original P/Q check, owned by root

Use the original Complementary archive and retained native398 world0 options,
WORLD_BLUR0 and MOTION_BLUR_EFFECT-1. Observe the actual RGB R11F_G11F_B10F
RT0 format rather than assuming the declaration. This test is untimed and
one-shot; it needs no candidate launch to falsify copy identity.

1. Reuse [SpatialCompositeMixin](../../src/devClient/java/com/pp/shaderlod/dev/mixin/SpatialCompositeMixin.java):
   its `createProgram` return receives exact ProgramSource and returned Program;
   its existing shadows include `pipeline`, `compositePass`, `passes` and
   `renderTargets`. Associate the precise named composite3 source/options and
   Program object in **CompositePass.COMPOSITE**. Existing SpatialLayoutProbe
   is DEFERRED/Photon-specific; a bounded root-owned extension must keep those
   guards intact rather than weakening them to accept this pack.
2. At [SpatialQuadMixin](../../src/devClient/java/com/pp/shaderlod/dev/mixin/SpatialQuadMixin.java)
   `renderQuad` HEAD, match CURRENT_PROGRAM to the named actual Pass, not only a
   numeric ID or filename. Record P from the active colortex0 sampler and Q from
   actual draw-framebuffer COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, including texture level0, object
   type, format/extents, viewport, blend/color-mask state and sampler parameters.
   Both must equal the two distinct IDs returned by `renderTargets.get(0)`;
   `stageReadsFromAlt` predicts which is input. Store renderer/pipeline/pack/
   frame identities, full effective options/source hashes and storage generation.
3. At **that exact quad RETURN**, recheck the same identities, then read full
   **P and Q level0 before composite4 starts**. The hook precedes composite4's
   `setupMipmapping`, unlike its later quad HEAD. Reading both physical images
   through `glGetTexImage` needs no replacement render/copy. Capture lossless
   packed RGB where supported, and a qualified numeric/alpha readback; report
   exact equality, differing texels/channels, maxima and nonfinite categories.
   Do not hide NaNs, conversion differences or border mismatches in a tolerance.
   Readback of RGB storage as RGBA supplies alpha1; it does not certify an
   arbitrary RGBA copy or arbitrary sampler state. Preserve and restore active
   texture/bindings, pack-PBO and all pack state (and any read-FBO/read-buffer
   state touched); restore on failure. Do not call `getOrCreate` or allocate a
   new target merely to inspect an existing one.
4. P/Q must belong to one storage lifetime. Object IDs can be reused after
   destruction, and resize can redefine storage while retaining IDs. Pair the
   same pipeline/RenderTargets/RenderTarget identities with actual extents and
   an allocation/resize generation; abort across reload, resize, dimension or
   pack changes. Existing frame/notifier source values are useful identifiers,
   not proof of synchronized candidate histories.

This is a **copy-primitive equality falsifier**. A passing original P/Q check
does not prove candidate graph, histories, final output, lifecycle or cost.
P and Q may legitimately have different old higher mip contents and filters
at this boundary: deferred1 can have generated one chain, composite3 writes
only level0, and composite4 will regenerate its selected current input. A raw
unused-mip mismatch alone is not an A6 failure.

Candidate work proof remains separate: composite3 must be absent from the
actual enabled graphics pass list **and** draw stream, with no compute companion,
replacement draw/blit/resolve or compensating final RT0 copy. Observe actual
RT0 clear membership and FinalPassRenderer swap list/calls; its exact
`lambda$new$1` returns for clear-listed targets, but a source expectation is not
an observed call absence. Verify composite4's regenerated input chain, subsequent
physical bindings and original/native/Off restoration. Whole-graph and lifecycle
acceptance still require matched logical outputs/history through first frame,
resize/reload, dimension return and supported DH/PBR paths. No dev Java,
instrumentation, client, project build, reload, world or GPU action was performed here.

## Cross-review and owner responses

| Challenge / concrete failure case | Owner response / disposition |
| --- | --- |
| BSL receiver: derivative hoist could follow a divergent material/discard branch or use a UV transform different from native bias | Inspected original main and GetShadow. Hoist follows worldPos in an unconditional block; PBR is excluded, DH/VOXY discarded path excluded. Earlier emission helpers reconverge and do not discard. SHADOW_PIXEL0/BIAS0 and no HALF_LAMBERT make UV identical; later native bias changes z only. Owner narrows an overbroad comment about earlier material divergence. Actual transformed shader's derivative/discard ordering remains a driver-source gate. |
| Both receivers: hardcoded outputPixelsPerRasterPixel1 would reduce too much under an external render scale | No native scale/size directives or TAAU remap found in these pins; TAA jitter preserves full-rate raster. Concrete helper case dx(.01,0), dy(0,.01), support(.001,.001) is plateau at scale1, native at scale4. Both owners accepted explicit actual physical raster-to-output ratio1 qualification; unsupported scaling retains native. Pack source alone cannot certify window/target scaling. |
| BSL custom uniform could register only in composite code, leaving terrain permission unbound | Exact [SodiumShader consumer bytecode](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r2/mips/receiver-custom-uniform-consumers.javap.txt) has buildUniforms→CustomUniforms.assignTo/mapholderToPass and updateUniforms→push. Sildur deferred uses CompositeRenderer's corresponding assign/push. Saved owner property/type bytecode resolves uniform.float through Type.Float and glUniform1f, distinct from enabled-property BooleanParser. Actual named draw, linked location and value1/0 remain required. |
| Uniform0 native-equivalent GLSL may let the driver avoid the classifier despite source-level derivatives being present | Both owners explicitly retain this limit. Same GLSL does not guarantee equal scheduling or evaluation of unused classifier inputs. No measured derivative overhead may be claimed without actual behavior/cost evidence. |
| Sildur nMap exposure could accidentally activate unrelated settings; derivatives could run inside land/sky/hand divergence | Original main is straight-line through fragpos0; the injected prelude precedes SSDO/handlight and land/sky/receiver branches. Native settings exposure is checked by owner's complete native preprocessor comparisons across AA/nMap and dimension/stage variants. Owner retains linked-source/map/encoding and actual uniform/viewport gates; no additional source blocker found in this bounded lens. |
| B13 quality peer: higher BASE_LEVEL/MIN_LOD could invalidate “explicit LOD0”; separate unsynchronized stills cannot prove TAA/history equality | Agreed. Actual base/LOD clamps, sampler0, physical ping-pong/filter/lifecycle and synchronized outputs remain gates. Current/history RT2 semantics and native jitter were traced; no new source blocker identified. |
| B13 cost peer: a removed c7 generation is not a removed draw or a known postprocess/total fraction | Agreed. c6 generation, graphics passes, targets and history remain native. Actual mip-set/call deletion, output proof and matched total cost are separate; there is no accepted speed estimate. |

The lead's parser challenge and both B13 peer responses are adopted, with no
unresolved disagreement. Receiver cross-review is a bounded source/resource
feasibility check; final owner artifact hashes and root runtime acceptance are
separate. Work remained within the assigned new files and ignored evidence;
no successor track or live resource was opened.

## Next experiment proposal (2026-10-04)

User is testing the core idea and prioritizes a substantial performance benefit.
Recommended sequence, not a newly approved goal or frozen numerical gate:

1. Attribute missing CPU/GPU cost: vanilla terrain layers, DH terrain/water,
   entities/translucency, frame submission, and existing shader passes. Identify
   GPU effect work versus geometry/bandwidth versus CPU limitation before adding
   more feature cuts. Existing GPU intervals include command-starvation gaps.
2. Test one realistic expensive preset/scene with useful enabled effects and
   identical settings for baseline/adaptive runs. Increasing both sides' settings
   is legitimate for testing the intended use case; artificially inflating only
   the baseline or choosing useless excess work is not evidence of value.
3. Compare original high, original lower quality, and high+adaptive LOD. The
   lower-quality control tests whether adaptive complexity adds value over a
   simple preset change. Target effects with multi-millisecond cost rather than
   collecting reductions in already-cheap effects. The Mac's reduced feature
   set does not establish performance for full desktop Photon.
4. A roughly15–20% GPU-render reduction is a suggested proof-of-concept target,
   subject to user choice and actual baseline budget. If the effect share cannot
   support that, report the ceiling. Extend into geometry/CPU work only after
   profiling establishes its relevance; that changes the project's scope.

Keep live comparison windows intact during analysis. No new experiment was
launched or performance threshold accepted solely by this proposal.

# Miniature 2.19 runtime and refinement experiment

Source-only plan, 2026-10-05, owner `pack_research`. Only this document was
created for this task. No candidate lock change, downloads, adapter code,
compiler, build or client launch. Initial Miniature rendering, integration,
support and performance remain unverified by this worker.

## Exact artifact and baseline

Use the existing [publisher release](https://modrinth.com/shader/miniature-shader/version/LWmZ94RG):
`miniature-shader-2.19.zip`, 43,913 bytes, SHA256
`5f224e907657f3ffd95d37e37c27e555deef64fa56da1e13374f2c295241d7f0`.
Publisher SHA512 already verified in `dev/shader-candidates.lock.json`. Read
the extracted **release**, `dev/upstream/other-pack-research/miniature-release/`,
not current upstream source: pinned Git `bdb6e0020b4318d4e845902cbcc3e3552b0e9274`
is not byte-identical to this release.

First launch: original archive, Minecraft 1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.253 / pinned
Iris 1.8.12 and Sodium 0.6.13 / Java 21 / Apple M3 Max, **DH physically absent**.
Use the existing minimal-stack workload and a shoreline with visible near and
far water plus reflected trees. Preserve the archive, effective Iris option map,
loaded artifacts/versions, camera, detail radius, window/pacing, weather/wetness,
time, screenshots and driver errors. The pack has no DH shader programs; do not
treat a no-DH render as DH compatibility.

The original source defaults match the pack's NORMAL profile. Preserve all
defaults initially; explicitly select NORMAL only if the option loader needs
a profile value. Essential recorded values are:

| Option | Original/default control | SSR refinement-only lower-quality control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SSR_MAX_STEPS` | `10` | `10` |
| `SSR_STEP_SIZE` | `1.6` | `1.6` |
| `SSR_BINARY_STEPS` | `4` | **`2`** |

## Program and feature requirements

The Overworld wrapper `shaders/world0/final.fsh` L1 uses `#version 120` and
includes `/program/final.fsh`. Its matching vertex program uses `ftransform()`
and a texture-coordinate varying. This relies on Iris's compatibility shader
translation; it is not a raw macOS core-context shader claim.

The final fragment declares four distinct samplers:

- `colortex0`: scene color, also sampled at the reflected hit.
- `colortex6`: encoded normal.
- `colortex7`: reflectivity, roughness and validity marker.
- `depthtex0`: opaque scene depth used for reconstruction and tracing.

`program/textured_lit.fsh` L130 and `program/translucent.fsh` L69 write
`DRAWBUFFERS:067`. Terrain shading separately uses texture/lightmap/shadowtex1;
translucent vertex shading samples the lightmap. Attachment index 7 does not
mean final uses eight samplers. Actual Iris-generated bindings/target formats
must be inspected in the loaded pipeline; the four source sampler declarations
alone are not a driver-link result.

No compute files, image-load/store code, custom-image requirements, explicit
mipmap-enable directives or DH programs were found in this release.
`shaders.properties` L40 lists optional `BLOCK_EMISSION_ATTRIBUTE`; it is not
a declared mandatory feature. For Minecraft 1.21.1, the `<12111` guards at
L42–45 disable gbuffers_line programs. Leave those upstream guards intact.
Baseline uses `texture2D` and existing matrix/depth helpers; no new texture or
framebuffer is needed for the refinement proposal. These observations suggest
a small source feature footprint, not established Apple compatibility.

## SSR behavior that must be preserved

`program/final.fsh` L23 masks SSR by reflectivity and a validity marker;
L38 reconstructs view position and L48 calls `getReflectionColor`.
`common/getReflectionColor.fsh` L11 computes reflected direction, rejecting
`R.z >= -0.05`. Its outer loop L24 has ten source-default iterations, offscreen
exit L28, and depth fetch/reconstruction L31–35. After each non-hit, L60 adds:

`max(SSR_STEP_SIZE * abs(diffZ) * invR, 1.0)`

This increment depends on sampled depth and ray direction. A five-step kernel
with doubled increment is **not** extent-preserving, equivalent to ten steps,
or guaranteed to retain the same first-hit bracket. Do not introduce that cut.

On the first `diffZ < 0` hit, L38–39 brackets `oldPos` and `curPos`. Only when
`diffZ > -16.0` does L42 refine the bracket with four midpoint depth samples.
The final guard L53 can discard a hit based on refined depth; L55 samples scene
color at the final refined UV. Thus reducing refinement leaves the outer march
and first bracket unchanged, but can change reflected color, hit acceptance and
edges. It is a quality approximation, not an exact optimization.

## Small proposed distance experiment

Prefer **4 near / 2 far binary refinements**, preserving all outer iterations,
step sizes, cutoffs, masks, reflected direction, roughness noise and miss return.
Only eligible first hits within the existing cutoff can save work: at most two
depth fetches per such hit. Many pixels miss, exit early, fail the mask or skip
refinement already; full-frame savings may be negligible. No gain is predicted
as an accepted result.

Compute one radial distance from reconstructed `viewPos` in camera/view-space
block units. `common/transformations.glsl` L62–63 unprojects normalized depth;
`view2feet` adds the model-view inverse translation, while `view2eye` only
applies its rotation. Use **`length(viewPos)` consistently with the existing
core protocol's camera/view-space distance convention**, not raw depth,
`abs(viewPos.z)`, absolute world position or the reflected ray's final hit
distance. Check third-person, view-bobbing and projection behavior in runtime;
do not silently mix feet-based distance with camera-based thresholds.

Initial diagnostic bands could retain four refinements through 96 blocks and
reach two at 160 blocks. They are candidate options for inspecting transitions,
not recommended defaults. A broad transition can select a midpoint budget of
three as well. Discrete budgets can create moving rings even when color/shadow
budgets are untouched. A useful diagnostic alternative performs a fixed maximum
of four refinements while retaining the second/fourth outcomes and blending
them smoothly; that tests transition quality but **saves no refinement fetches**.
If that quality diagnostic fails, stop before benchmarking a cheap variant.

For a savings variant, prefer reviewed literal refinement kernels or a
well-bounded uniform maximum with early exit; test the generated shader rather
than assuming a dynamic loop compiles cheaply. Do not run both complete SSR
paths per pixel and label the blend an optimization. A world-stable budget
selector can spread a transition, but without a demonstrated temporal filter
it can create grain/edge crawling. No new per-frame random dithering is proposed.

Noise already comes from `common/math.glsl::random3` L9, applied at
`program/final.fsh` L45 to quantized `worldPos`. The quantization scale changes
with feet-position distance through 16 blocks (L41–42), and roughness zero leaves
water unperturbed. Preserve this behavior: adding time-dependent noise or
changing quantization would confound refinement quality and performance.

**Derivative limit:** existing `texture2D` calls occur inside nonuniform masks,
ray exits and hit branches. Adding distance-selected refinement introduces
another source of divergent texture access. Implicit derivatives in such
control flow cannot be used as a correctness argument. A modified active path
should use a verified explicit base-level depth/color sampling form, or provide
reviewed valid gradients. GLSL 1.20 fragment explicit-LOD syntax is not guaranteed
by the original version declaration; check pinned Iris translation/driver
support before adopting `texture2DLod`/`textureLod`. No mipmap-enable directive
was found, but verify actual allocated mip levels/filtering before asserting
base-level fetches reproduce existing sampling. Keep a preprocessed original
path for adapter-off; do not globally rewrite all pack samples in this experiment.

# Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

For the prepared RTX 2080 Ti Windows host, see [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md).

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py baseline --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --output FRESH_BASELINE
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`baseline` renders the original pack with the main mod absent in the backed-up
authored save. After 120 seconds conditioning it captures three unchanged
20-second native windows, with the standard ownership, readiness, sample and
restoration checks. The report gives frame sample variance/SD (ms²/ms), and
separately variance/SD of the three window means and first-to-last drift.
These describe frame jitter and within-process variation, respectively; neither
is a confidence interval. Repeat in fresh processes to measure between-run
variation. Keep absent-mod baselines separate from the matched Master-Off
controls in optimization comparisons. Startup failure supplies no frame-time
measurement. `native-startup` remains a short original-only startup diagnostic.

`--gl-context native` preserves Minecraft's normal context request. For explicit
desktop API coverage, maintained comparisons also accept `3.2`, `4.3`, `4.5` and
`4.6`. These request real GLFW contexts; they do not override reported versions
or capabilities. Explicit requests disable NeoForge's reusable early window in
the owned profile, with the normal configuration backup/CAS/restoration contract.
The returned desktop version must meet the requested minimum and is recorded in
`summary.json.gl_context`. A driver returning4.6 for a4.5 request is labeled4.6;
it does not supply an independent4.5 result. Keep actual context/configuration
cohorts and their native baselines separate. Frozen Bliss qualification retains
its existing native-context protocol and refuses an explicit context override.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

The command automatically selects the existing Linux ARM64 launcher on that platform. Explicit `linux_arm64_runtime.py` commands remain supported. It finds an installed full JDK21 or a cached Gradle JDK21; an explicit JAVA_HOME retains precedence. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

C02 is an explicitly labeled 2×2 bloom quality tradeoff, with Master-On native
controls; its scoped exception is documented in the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md#c02-experimental-bloom-shading-rate).

| Question | Maintained route | What it does not establish |

| What inputs and candidates exist? | `discover`, then `plan` with selected inputs | Runtime compatibility or ownership |

## Requested work and count conversions

[work_policy.glsl](../shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/work_policy.glsl:57)
validates transported bands, protocols, integer count domain and legal floor.
It computes `continuous_requested_work = upstream_work * ratio`, then ceil and
floor-clamps an integer `realized_work`. The volume consumer intentionally uses
the continuous request instead of that rounded integer.

[volume_budget.glsl](../shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/volume_budget.glsl:12)
requires `1 <= minimum <= original <= 65536` before uint→int conversions.
It returns `target = clamp(mix(N, N*r, w), minimum, N)`, where
`w = footprint_weight * (1 - protected_weight)` lies in [0,1] for validated
inputs. Thus target cannot exceed N. The frozen consumer obtains N by uint
conversion of the direction-dependent 40→20 mix, matching the original selected
DEFERRED1 stage's truncation. The `/2` DEFERRED0 counts inside the copied body
are inactive: manifest injection explicitly selects DEFERRED1 and excludes the
atmosphere-transmittance LUT. This conclusion depends on those stage guards.

The active loop uses `uint(ceil(target))`, so its *maximum* primary iterations
also cannot exceed integer N. For N=39 and ratio .75, target=29.25 means 30
cells, a 23.08% cap reduction. A transition or a partially restored quality
weight can reduce target by less than one without reducing the integer cap at
all, while still selecting the active path and changing its grid. Far .75 and
medium .85 are requests; near, overhead, insufficient footprint and fallback
can restore full work. There is no count overflow or deliberate budget→density
conversion in the validated frozen path. The policy is evaluated once in
preflight and again with actual distance/quality; preflight results are not the
executed cell count.

## What changes physical work

The diff against `000f355^` shows the shared-system change alters policy,
capability checks and radial entry calculation. The copied march, density,
secondary optical-depth and continuous-cell helpers are unchanged from that
prior implementation. INHERIT previously used private .85/.75; it now resolves
unity and therefore selects original. ADAPTIVE delegates to the common policy.

Compared with original Photon, the following integration differences matter:

- **Early exits remain data dependent.** Both bodies return on zero coverage,
  blocked/missed shell and terrain, skip empty density, and break when running
  transmittance falls below .075. Primary density has shell/coverage-map bounds
  and an altitude-shaped density exit before its two Worley samples. Changing
  sample locations changes all these outcomes. An active path with cap 30 can
  execute more cells than an original cap-40 path that broke after one cell.
- **Sampling positions change with the continuous target.** Original samples
  are `entry + (i + jitter)*L/N`. Active samples are
  `entry + i*L/target + jitter*cell_length(i)`. For integer targets these are
  equal-width grids at the new spacing; for fractional targets the final cell
  is shorter and its jitter is restricted to that remaining cell. The cell
  lengths sum to L in real arithmetic. They do not preserve original density
  occupancy, optical depth or the transmittance-break index in a varying field.
  The same frame dither input is used; positions and the per-cell `hash2` that
  dithers secondary rays change. There is no new stochastic count selector.
- **Secondary work is not reduced independently.** Each primary cell surviving
  the density check executes six direct-light and two ambient density calls,
  then the original eight-iteration scattering approximation. Those secondary
  loops have no optical-depth early break. Executed density-call count is
  `P + 8*Q`, with P reached primary cells and Q cells entering lighting. A lower
  P cap does not imply a lower Q. The density function itself can exit before
  detail, so even this call count does not prove equal texture or ALU cost.
- **No new lighting-strength normalization shortcut.** Active extinction uses
  `density * extinction_coeff * cell_length`; the original scattering integral
  `(1 - step_transmittance)/extinction_coeff` remains. Cell-length-weighted
  apparent-distance accumulators replace equal-width accumulators, needed for
  the partial cell. For a uniform field and no early truncation this preserves
  total optical thickness. It does not restore exact heterogeneous lighting,
  because density, secondary hash, ray origin and break location changed.
- **Selected and fallback paths execute one complete march.** Wrapper lines
  373–450 return either original or active; they do not evaluate both results
  and mix them. However, active-eligible rays evaluate spherical-shell
  intersection in the wrapper and again in the selected inner body. Rays that
  later fall back also repeat that setup in original. Coverage-zero is checked
  after wrapper shell intersection, while original checks it before setup.
  The wrapper does not prove planet occlusion before footprint/sampler queries;
  the inner body may immediately reject such a ray. Disabled/FULL/unity and
  capability-invalid paths return before these expensive wrapper steps.
- **Additional per-cell arithmetic is explicit.** Active cells compute a
  clamped remaining length and a sampled position; the cell sample helper
  itself recomputes cell length. Constant fold/common-subexpression elimination
  may remove some arithmetic, but source inspection cannot prove that driver
  result. Inlined original and active functions also increase compiled-program
  alternatives; branch/register/compiler effects remain unmeasured.
- **Sampler fetches are conditional on density, not work eligibility alone.**
  Shared helpers fetch no textures. Wrapper `textureSize` is metadata query,
  not a texture-value fetch. Once shaped density survives, both Worley fetches
  are written unconditionally even if a runtime weight were zero; this was
  already true upstream. Local coverage writes two noisetex reads, but the
  pilot has PRECOMPUTE_LOCAL_COVERAGE=true and uses one coverage-map fetch
  instead. Active density and secondary calls use explicit `textureLod(...,0)`
  where original uses implicit `texture(...)`; local coverage does likewise.
  This distinction predates the shared-policy refactor. Prior untimed QA
  reports linear sampling, no sampler objects and LOD-0 noise allocations; it
  does not establish equal instruction cost or fresh timed-arm sampler state.

## Numerical and derivative objections to challenge in the exact patch

For the BSL candidate, set `a = 0.0476*CLOUD_DETAIL`, `b = noiseBase`,
`d = noiseDetail`, `c = noiseCoverage`, `r = 0.33*rainStrength` and
`s = 3*sunCoverage + CLOUD_AMOUNT`. Native pre-clamp density is

`F(b,d,c,r,s) = mix(21*mix(b,d,a)-c, 21-2.5*c, r)-s`.

For native finite option ranges, `0 < a < 1`, `0 <= r <= 0.33`, and normalized
linear-filtered noise has `0 <= d <= 1`. Thus `F(b,1,c,r,s)` bounds the native
value from above. A strictly negative, roundoff-safe bound certifies zero before
`CloudApplyDensity`, with no volume approximation or altered sample interval.
The exact patch passes the independent float32/source checks above while keeping
the driver-precision boundary explicit. Sampling an arbitrary
floating texture or accepting extrapolated rain/detail values would invalidate
the stated input envelope.

The two native detail lookups are implicit `texture2D` operations. A per-lane
early return before those calls creates new divergent control flow. The GLSL
specification leaves implicit derivatives undefined in such flow; existing
native divergence is not proof that another divergent path is harmless.
[Khronos GLSL 4.10, texture lookup functions](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/GLSLangSpec.4.10.pdf).
R2 uses explicit level zero in the eligible detail branch under the pinned
non-mipmapped sampler contract. Moving
derivative instructions into an already divergent native loop is not a general
derivative-safety proof.

BSL `texture.noise=tex/noise.png`; its metadata requests blur and repeat. Prior
actual deferred1 evidence on the historical MC 1.21.1 NeoForge tuple records
512×512 RGBA8, min/mag LINEAR, base/max level zero, anisotropy one, bias zero,
sampler zero. This supports reuse of that implementation contract, not proof
of the future changed primary draw or another loader.
[Actual prior readback and identity limits](bsl-reflected-cloud-distance-cue-runtime-r2-review.md).
R2 retains a real source/native fallback outside its scope. Fresh inspection of
the pinned Iris Fabric 1.11.4 bytecode also follows the PNG metadata through
`NativeImageBackedCustomTexture.getSampling()` to `GlSampler.LINEAR_REPEAT`:
min/mag LINEAR, no mipmapping, repeat and comparison disabled. This supports the
source premise on the future Fabric tuple; actual bound texture/sampler state
and target-driver filtering parity still need an observation after resume.

The base lookup occurs before the new density rejection branch. The per-lane
numeric-domain fallback calls the native function and relies on the same
non-mipmapped sampler envelope; it is not a general claim that implicit texture
derivatives become defined for arbitrary unsupported samplers. Ordinary native
finite inputs satisfy these guards. DH, Voxy, advanced materials, other cloud
types/bases and other dimensions compile out the new helper; weather, Core and
preset exclusions return natively before coordinate work. Rain is deliberately
restricted to exactly zero in this new, pretrial design.

discarded: for default amount 10, gradient 0–1, rain 0–1 and sun coverage 0–1,

`3K - 2R + F`, versus native
`3K`. A late fallback has already fetched the base once before repeating the
native call. With ordinary finite native inputs `F=0`; the source reduction is

`int(min(...,32)+1)`. No image-space or GPU invocation census was collected.

Original/patched-disabled/active captured roughly 139.87/139.33/113.05 FPS and 6.58/6.54/8.135 ms GPU mean in that short pilot. Active still changes clouds, fog, SSR and water together. The two inspected screenshots show the same shoreline and shadows; the active cloud sky looks more finely grained. Static captures cannot distinguish moving shimmer from one temporal/noise phase. Water normals also differ visibly as expected, and the real animation clocks differ. Neither observation assigns the slowdown. ## The original near function is mathematically preserved but not source-preserved Original `include/surface/water_normal.glsl:get_water_height` has two loops with `i < WATER_WAVE_ITERATIONS`, a fixed-length noise array and a const normalization based on that compile-time macro. Original `get_water_normal` calls it three times. Original water parallax calls it initially and in its depth-march while loop. For the current option, the compiler sees the literal budget 3 in every height evaluation and can unroll the noise/math loops, use statically indexed array elements and precompute constants. Actual Apple driver lowering is not available from source alone, so eligibility is not proof of unrolling. The 218992b patch changed height's signature to accept `int wave_iterations`, both loop bounds to that parameter, array indexing to the corresponding runtime index and normalization to a runtime exponent. Current 7ca retains that design. Even near/disabled normal calls pass a variable produced by the LOD budget helper into those functions. The current finite path reproduces original values when that variable equals 3, but it does not literally call the untouched fixed 3 function. The comment "exact original evaluation" refers to operation/results, not the compiler's original constant-loop code shape. That distinction matters. An active per-pixel tier changes iterations across fragments. A compiler can choose dynamic loops, extra bounds/index machinery, register-backed array storage or predicated iterations rather than statically unrolling a literal 3. Parallax nests these height loops inside its own variable-step while loop, amplifying any such lowering difference. This is a plausible cost mechanism, not evidence that the driver currently spills registers or executes extra work. The patched-off pilot being close to original also means a universal pack-wide dynamic-loop penalty is not established; enabled divergence/cheap-path lowering or unrelated phase/work changes remain possible. Analytic gradients have a dynamic loop too, no temporary wave array, but sine and cosine rather than height's sine alone. Mixing analytic and finite paths across the 80–112-block transition can make adjacent lanes execute different algorithms; the original full path may still execute in some lanes even if most pixels request cheap normals. A low sample count therefore does not guarantee low wall/GPU time. Water at 160 blocks also retains new medium parallax whereas old generic 32/96 LOD skipped it. The new conservative policy intentionally keeps more nearby detail and work. ## Proposed static specialization, without changing the selected effect First isolate the loop structure with finite differences only. Preserve the entire pinned original get_water_height/get_water_normal/get_water_parallax_coord functions and their original names/signatures/bodies. Shadow calls continue to use them directly. Add LOD wrappers and cheap helpers rather than teaching the original helpers to accept a runtime iteration count. - A wrapper classifies quality once for surface normal, and once for parallax. Tier 0 or disabled explicitly calls the original function. Unsupported bridge versions retain the current pack-option fallback before tier selection. Near geometry still has the original 3-bound height loops and original constant 4 parallax budget in this profile. - Cheap helper bodies use a compile-time integer macro/literal for each supported octave count, not `const int` function parameters. GLSL parameter const means non-assignable; it does not require a compile-time call value. An explicit specialization gives the compiler literal bounds/indexes and allows fixed normalization. It still does not force a driver optimization. - Runtime preset can change through the live bridge, so emit the finitely many counts required by Balanced/Performance/Aggressive for the configured original macro, then dispatch at the wrapper. Their origin is `entry + step_length*dither` and every sample advances by that coarser stride. The full clipped ray extent remains covered statistically; this is not simply truncating the original fine march. Coarser density integration can miss thin features, change opacity termination, apparent cloud distance and temporal reprojection. Preserved ray extent does not establish preserved image quality. Secondary rays grow steps geometrically by 2. The compensation preserves total extent when reducing O original steps to N: ```text new_initial_length = (C/N) * (N/O) * (2^O - 1)/(2^N - 1) original_total_extent = 2*(C/O)*(2^O - 1) new_total_extent = 2*new_initial_length*(2^N - 1) ``` The totals agree, but the coarser locations and quadrature weights do not. Lower secondary counts can cause noisy cloud lighting even with preserved optical-depth extent. The compensation uses runtime exp2 and division per secondary-ray call; literal-count specializations could precompute it, but that is a separate cloud control, not proof water loops caused this pilot. # ShaderLOD project overview

## Current product scope — 2026-10-07

The latest approved direction is shared rendering work avoidance with small
explicit adapters, Photon as the deeper reference, and parallel support for
Complementary Reimagined/Unbound, BSL, MakeUp Ultra Fast, Sildur’s Vibrant,
Solas, Bliss and AstraLex. NeoForge and Fabric retain Minecraft 1.21.1 and now
also target 1.21.11, 26.1.2, 26.2 and 26.3, explicitly added by the human on
2026-10-06. Modern versions use Iris/OpenGL; Vulkan is deferred. Development and runtime
testing are Mac-only for now; preserve Windows setup/evidence without SSH or
Prism changes. Verify each loader/Iris/toolchain and actual rendered integration
independently; available renderer APIs do not themselves prove shader support.
Users keep their shader preset and choose an LOD Performance/Balanced/Quality
preset; Off keeps full quality for that shader preset. Detect supported versions,
preserve installed originals, and generate separate adapter copies. Iris remains
required, DH optional for users, DH/PBR compatibility required. Target macOS,
Linux and Windows; identify actual tested hardware rather than implying coverage.

Short fullscreen performance sanity checks and representative visual inspection
now guide iteration; precision benchmark gates must not block unrelated product
work. The older development sequence and scope below are retained history and
are superseded where they conflict. The compact STATUS/active goal govern work.

ShaderLOD targets general-purpose, configurable distance quality control across
shader packs. Photon is the first implementation and performance proof. The first platform is NeoForge with Iris required. Photon is the
explicit compatibility target, and DH is optional for the mod while included
in the development runtime for compatibility checks.

The initial distance proposal is full quality through 32 blocks, medium quality
through 96 blocks, and low quality beyond that. These are starting defaults,
not a measured optimum. Define distance in camera-relative block units and
use transition bands or stable dithering to avoid a visible moving ring.

## Development sequence

1. Establish a reproducible NeoForge client skeleton and compatible Iris,
   Sodium, Photon, and DH runtime. Add durable goal/team infrastructure and a
   small LOD foundation that can be inspected and tested.
2. Prove one distance-sensitive Photon effect works under Iris with DH absent.
   Compare the same scene with the change disabled and enabled; inspect both
   visual transitions and GPU execution time before expanding infrastructure.
3. Build the Photon MVP around several measured effects. Candidate effects are
   POM/material work, shadow filtering, and SSR. Add validated configuration
   transport and useful quality presets as evidence supports them.
4. Extend LOD to DH terrain/water/shadows and validate the vanilla/DH boundary.
   Keep DH optional and test both installed and absent configurations.

## Architecture boundaries

The NeoForge client mod owns config, loader/runtime detection, and integration
lifecycle. Photon owns explicit GLSL LOD logic through a pinned, maintained
patch or derivative. Iris provides the shader runtime. DH extends terrain
rendering and eventually needs dedicated integration checks.

A Java config file does not automatically become an Iris custom uniform.
Document and test the actual bridge before claiming the mod controls shader
quality live. Shader-pack options can support the first proof independently.
Do not expand into automatic rewriting of arbitrary shader packs during setup.

## Product direction clarified by the user

The intended product eventually supports many shaders through a common Iris LOD
protocol, per-effect configuration and explicit pack adapters. Configuration can
map options, units, budgets, compatibility and defaults. Each shader still needs
reviewed code that avoids effect work with distance; names or preset changes alone
do not establish that connection. Pin and verify adapters independently.

Renderer-specific CPU experiments remain secondary, optional components. They
must not become the product's main abstraction or change sunlight cadence to
manufacture results. No sunlight updates or shadow-map refreshes have been changed;
source cadence investigation only informs possible visibility reuse. Photon stays
the reference implementation. The latest 2026-10-05 user direction focuses
development on general LOD and adjacent work avoidance, reusable integration
interfaces and little discernible quality loss, with Photon as the only supported
shader. Other-pack experiments are retained historical evidence. Additional pack
implementation is outside the current goal; future support still requires each
pack's own compilation, rendering, repeated timing and quality evidence.

## Initial risks

Distance branches may save little GPU work when neighboring pixels diverge.
Some effects cannot safely change samples or ray-march steps without changing
appearance or temporal stability. Loader and renderer versions must be
compatible as a set. Photon may require hardware/driver features unavailable
on the development Mac; record this as a runtime limit rather than calling
static source inspection a rendering pass.

The setup goal establishes an environment and evidence base. It does not
promise an FPS gain, freeze the product's final quality thresholds, or complete
the later Photon/DH MVP.

records.text:
# Reflection footprint refinement LOD reference adapter

Source freeze 2026-10-05. Independent reflection implementation track; owns only
this report, `scripts/build_photon_reflection_lod.py`,
`tests/test_photon_reflection_lod.py`,
`patches/photon-experiments/reflection-lod.json`, and
`shaderpacks/photon-reflection-lod/**`. Other workers own Java, shared shader
helpers and other experiments. Root owns client/reloads/GPU; this worker ran
no client, Gradle, GLSL driver compiler, GPU query or image processing.

## Implemented behavior

A transferable distance/projected-footprint policy shortens binary reflection
refinement only when remaining spatial uncertainty is bounded. Full original
intersection count, sampled ray positions, extent, dither, depth tolerance,
projection/depth sampler and environment coverage remain. No untraced far segment
is replaced with sky. Both smooth-water and rough reflection callers use this
adapter; original rough ray counts, BSDF factors and accumulation normalization
remain. The separate original raytracer stays byte-identical, so AO/SSGI callers
are unaffected. There is no hierarchy/new pass/new target allocation.

Entry points are original `trace_specular_ray` in
`shaders/include/lighting/specular_lighting.glsl` and new
`shaderlod_reflection_depth_trace` / `shaderlod_raymarch_depth_cached` in
`shaders/include/shaderlod/reflection_depth_cache.glsl`. Compile option
`SHADERLOD_REFLECTION_DEPTH_CACHE` is default off; its name includes the
secondary exact integer-depth reuse path. Pinned settings and the single
specular caller are the only changed original members; one helper is added.
Original Photon v1.3b by Benjamin Stott (SixthSurge), original LICENSE retained.

Activation requires core protocol2, global enable exactly1, finite nonnegative
near/far/transition with far>near and 0<width<=far-near, finite receiver distance,
valid original dither, positive original budgets and bounded supported counts
(intersection<=256, refinement<=64). Unknown/absent mod, disabled bridge, invalid
policy/counts and full near execute the literal upstream tracer. These are
source-consumed core fields; live uniform linkage/reload remains unverified.
Extension1 per-effect fields, debug and preset are not consumed. No pack option
is represented as an actually verified mod connection.

Distance is Euclidean camera-relative view space in Minecraft blocks. Below
near+width/2 (default36 blocks), the original trace executes. Smoothstep from
near+width/2 to far+width/2 (default36..100 blocks) increases tolerated remaining
hit displacement from zero to0.25 depth-texture texel. The transition is continuous
in error tolerance; discrete iteration changes still require motion QA.
Footprint is calculated explicitly from the projected ray step and effective
view resolution/TAAU scale, without derivatives or implicit LOD sampling.

At least one original refinement update executes before stopping. Every possible
remaining original position must fit inside the same valid fetched depth texel
with conservative boundary margins. Thus its sampled hand/sky/terrain depth and
original final-depth eligibility are preserved. In addition, the entire remaining
z envelope must lie uniformly inside/outside the original depth-hit predicate
with a margin, projected UV displacement must be<=0.25texel, and remaining screen
depth uncertainty<=1/16 original depth tolerance. Screen depth is nonlinear:
two endpoints of the actual ray segment and current point are inverse-projected
using the same Photon helper as final hit composition. Homogeneous W must have
no pole, and the conservative Euclidean view displacement must stay within0.049block, reserving1mm toward
a0.05block cap. Near/far view displacement must not be inferred from NDC error.
This bound does not prove perceptual parity of reprojected color or fog.

A secondary cache reuses only the immediately preceding valid integer texel's
LOD0 depth before issuing `texelFetch`; invalid/out-of-range fetches are never
reused. Original ray arithmetic and every coarse hit test remain. First refinement
can reuse its just-found coarse depth. Thin edges, different texels and failed
error/classification envelopes continue the original refinement updates. No ray
weights or normalization change, and original sky/environment/fog composition is
retained. Fixed-depth source assumptions require immutable sampled attachment
through a draw, as original explicit depthtex1/combined depth usage intends.

## Static acceptance and exact artifacts

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_photon_reflection_lod.py -v`
passed9 tests, no skips. Coverage: literal disabled original spec/settings bytes,
unchanged raytracer/license, original coarse loop/weights/composition, fail-closed
pins/scope/errors, near/fallback policy,3000 exact cache models,5000 bounded
refinement/hand/sky/error models, undefined-coordinate nonreuse, deterministic
archive/license/member-scope assembly, and actual pinned Iris
OptionAnnotatedSource/OptionSet/MutableOptionValues option discovery/defaults/both
overrides. The private gate is the sole new boolean option; stage macro does not
leak. The actual lexer fixture uses local Java source launcher, no Gradle/download
or GLSL driver compilation. Scalar fixtures use host double arithmetic and simple
perspective; they do not establish every GLSL float rounding or DH/TAAU matrix.

Original archive SHA256:
`120897768eaa8cb1f14a3e98f88dff009ae3204ee3b96904a4fe8586edfc1ead`.
Original LICENSE SHA256:
`514402d18eedb0afe374344ca9f0fe87b7399779518184b8fc64e31674555fc5`.
Manifest:
`0c20609c50ee65d98ec803eb96294a0d727bff82d81a6634abb1504518d89e1a`.
Helper:
`b5dd57b6f6155ada9489416ad94c5b4be00286615b9fce71ecf09400968ca44a`.
Default-off archive `build/Photon-ReflectionFootprintLOD-disabled.zip`:
`d11de4c94fb58520e9972a816e9739486fa8578b876fbd20c17aa933a4a82e16`.
Explicit-on source archive `build/Photon-ReflectionFootprintLOD-enabled.zip`:
`38b892a9ff4de1c19c77198ff8d3f553ada4ed070d7ea274d0e79a09ab602fe1`.
Both have2 modified original members,529 unchanged original members, one added
helper and private metadata. Builders reject nonignored outputs, unknown archive,
unsafe/duplicate ZIP paths, changed source/license/helper and unknown control arms.
Generated archives remain ignored. Source-off means upstream paths; global-off
with the option compiled still includes wrapper validation overhead.

## Runtime stopping boundary and needed measurement

count, v the native direction after curvature, H=100 the layer height. Native
geometric increment is `Δx = v H/(abs(v.y) N)`, while the optical multiplier is
`h = length(v 90/(abs(v.y) N))`. The **90 versus 100 ratio is intentional native
calibration** and must be preserved. Changing the count before both denominators

```
t_i = exp(-h μ_i)
C_(i+1) = C_i + L_i (1 - t_i) T_i
T_(i+1) = T_i t_i
```

# Benchmark guide

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

On Linux ARM64 use `python3 scripts/linux_arm64_runtime.py benchmark test` with the same arguments. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

G01 MakeUp copy elimination and G02 BSL mip elimination also collect existing untimed work witnesses after each measurement, disarming them before further timing. The BSL witness requires a separate untimed reload; inspect its completeness rather than inferring execution from parsed directives. G04 MakeUp `translucent_fastpath` requires `--saved-pose 9`: the maintained caller places one honey block in the backed-up save before all arms to cover the non-water/glass translucent class. Client visibility is checked; whole-save restoration removes the fixture after shutdown, including failed runs. Use `--width` and `--height` for the actual fullscreen mode (currently 2560×1600 on the local Asahi display).

The standard test records the prepared profile’s resource-pack file identities and freezes its selection requests. It requires those requests to be loaded before conditioning and checks the same actual selection before every arm; silent incompatible-pack removal refuses timing. Selection is enforced at those boundaries; resource bytes are not continuously rehashed. Saved pose11 is a close view of the existing stone gallery for native PBR material coverage.

G03 MakeUp early-alpha captures existing qualified-draw counters in snapshots and its untimed source/admission diagnostic after each arm. The permission-based route requires an admitted context beforehand and qualified-counter progress afterward; these are admission counts, not avoided fragments. The Asahi post-sample route has no draw permission: it instead requires the typed rewrite receipt and all current source/input checks. Its timing remains explicitly source-setup-only evidence, without linked consumption or fragment coverage proof. CPU-cost profiling remains disabled for ordinary plans.

BSL reflection and AO sample-reuse tests retain untimed draw-admission status; admission is not a saved-query count. Photon is validated by its separate pinned live-pixel-budget producer and manifest. Its generated solid-terrain program marker is checked at its exact declared value; unknown added options and changes to original native options still fail.

The standard test also accepts `--candidate c01-bounds` without `--feature` for the existing finite private extra-occlusion prototype. It requires the exact original MakeUp9.5g/native100 map and no DH. Both controls and the candidate retain master Off with empty public requests; only the private current-frame query mode changes (prefix1, groups32). Actual query/read progress is required before and after candidate timing. This is separate from public depth priming.

Use `--candidate g10-exact-bloom` without `--feature` for the finite private MakeUp exact zero-dither bloom reuse variant. It preserves native100 and four original additions, and requires an actual pre-detach compile/link receipt joined to consuming bloom draws. The original pack is used for both Off controls. Staged private packs and sidecars are backed up/restored by the operation; diagnostic reloads acknowledge rendered readiness and settled configuration. An integer work image runs after all three timed arms, with its actual writer texture joined to readback. Source-expression opportunity counts are not hardware-fetch savings. `--candidate g10-native-control` uses the same private producer with selector0 and requires native linked source; it is explicitly labeled a known-null control, with descriptive timing retained and no optimization conclusion.

The experimental combination command accepts `--features dead_frame_copy,ao_attenuation` instead of `--feature` for the current MakeUp G01/G06 pair. It enables an explicit benchmark-only admission switch, retains the original native100/API/platform/source checks, requires both requested compile controls, a selected G06 source marker matching each arm, and complete G01 executed-copy witnesses (6/3/6 per completed final pass). Candidate copy coverage is checked before timing as well as afterward. Ordinary clients retain singleton guards; other combinations are refused until separately supported. This is an initial combination experiment, not an all-twelve-active configuration or a claim of global optimality.

If the harness or inputs fail, preserve the failure, restore/release owned resources, fix the maintained harness or inputs, and retry. Do not copy harness code into report-local callers, inject launcher overrides, relax admission after failure, or substitute custom scripts for the standard result. Diagnostics are diagnostic and do not replace it. One Linux ARM64 BSL standard run completed with verified restoration and independent review; this does not establish behavior for other configurations or future changes. See [experiment history](EXPERIMENTS.md).

Keep reports, worlds, downloads, builds and captures out of Git. Do not kill unrelated processes. If restoration refuses due to unknown changes, preserve the data and inspect ownership and recovery before acting.

Runtime dependencies and original shader-pack inputs are stored under `dependencies/`. Keep active experiment output in `dev/experiments/` and any retained evidence in `experiment-evidence/`; both are local and outside Git. Prepared clients and worlds remain under `run-workloads/`.

## Exact change and quality budget

Each private function is a literal copy of the original SSR function, changing
only its name, the binary-refinement loop bound to4/3/2, and all its depth/color
fetches to explicit base-level syntax. Outer loop, adaptive increment
max(SSR_STEP_SIZE*abs(diffZ)*invR,1.0), reflected direction, offscreen exit,
epsilon/cutoffs, oldPos/curPos hit bracket, vignette/fresnel, final depth guard
and miss result are retained. Original native function and sampling syntax
remain intact. No light/shadow budgets change.

Mode2 computes one length(viewPos) from the originating reconstructed
camera/view-space position in Minecraft blocks. Near clamps to0; far clamps to
at least near+1. At/below near selects4, strictly between near/far selects3,
at/beyond far selects2. It is not feet length, raw depth, axial z, world origin,
reflected hit distance or time-varying noise. Integer transitions are stable for
a fixed camera but can create moving rings; this is deliberately not advertised
as a smooth quality transition. Root must inspect crossings and stop promotion
if quality fails. No second full SSR path or complete-path blend executes.

Only an eligible first hit inside the existing refinement cutoff saves samples:
at most one depth refinement fetch in the middle zone, two in the far zone.
Outer march coverage and first-hit bracket stay intact, but final refined UV,
hit acceptance, thin geometry and reflected color can change. Many pixels miss
or skip refinement already, so full-frame savings may be negligible. Near/full4
uses new fetch syntax and cannot be called exact pixel parity until mode1 versus
original is compared on the driver. All three literal copies enlarge source;
inlining, register allocation and instruction-cache effects can offset savings.
Mode1 allows the compiler to discard unused2/3 copies, so its code shape is not
a complete control for every mode2 compiler effect.

# Automatic DH coverage: feasibility and staged design

2026-10-04. Research only; no automatic coverage implementation or runtime proof.
The inspected artifact is DH 3.3.3 for Minecraft 1.21.1, SHA1
`4357b4d19fab818780c94f0e43dad1cc931634b2`, pinned in
`dev/runtime.lock.json`. Findings below come from `javap -c -p` on that binary.
Temporary disassembly is in `/tmp/shaderlod-coverage-audit/`, outside Git.

**Decision:** a bounded internal adapter can report nominal uploaded section
footprints, but a read-only poll of the existing quadtree/buffer fields cannot
conservatively certify a complete replacement ring. Missing per-column source
provenance and mutation epochs are the principal blockers. Keep manual opt-in
and travel revocation. If automatic geometry policy becomes the next priority,
first add a diagnostic observer, then version-pinned metadata/lifecycle hooks;
never activate from a ready-section count or repeated matching counts.
