DH’s public terrain/render API offers no equivalent complete uploaded-ring
summary; see [DH_COVERAGE_AUDIT.md](DH_COVERAGE_AUDIT.md). Public repository reads
can block and do not establish render completion.

## Why uploaded footprints alone are insufficient

`FullDataToRenderDataTransformer.transformCompleteFullDataToColumnData` iterates
64×64 source columns. Despite its name, the helper
`updateOrReplaceRenderDataViewColumnWithFullDataColumn` simply returns for a null
or empty column. The surrounding transformer can still return a non-empty
`ColumnRenderSource`, so part of a section may be absent while other columns
produce geometry. `FullDataSourceV2.isEmpty=false` means something exists, not
that all columns are complete.

Source metadata includes `FullDataSourceV2.columnGenerationSteps` and per-column
data lists. It is not retained by `LodBufferContainer`. The transformer caller
`LodRenderSection.getRenderSourceForPos` closes the full data source after
conversion; later meshes therefore cannot be audited by reading a retained
source object. Re-querying the database can return a different revision and
incur storage work. `DOWN_SAMPLED` and “known empty air” also need explicit
semantics; “some non-air vertices” is not a substitute. The pinned downsampling
helper `determineMinWorldGenStepForTwoByTwoColumn` takes a numeric minimum, but
other merge paths can assign `DOWN_SAMPLED`. A completeness proof must trace
those paths and never assume that one enum value certifies all child columns.

## Lifecycle and race constraints

`LodQuadTree.tryTick` uses `treeTickLock.tryLock()`. During its update, the tree
builds an alternate enabled list, swaps lists under `enabledRenderSectionLock`,
then disables/deletes other nodes. Holding the enabled-list lock protects list
publication, not every section/container operation.

Upload completion in `LodRenderSection.lambda$uploadToGpuAsync$0` replaces the
section’s container, closes the old container and clears dirty state.
`LodBufferContainer.close()` clears `buffersUploaded` and queues render-thread
cleanup that nulls/closes wrapper entries. `LodRenderSection.close()` disables
rendering, cancels work and closes a container without necessarily clearing its
reference. Thus non-null, upload-complete or twice-equal snapshots are not
sufficient liveness proofs. Do not call build/upload/close methods from an
observer, acquire a section monitor that can block on its synchronized builder,
retain VBO references for later use, or inspect GL state to recover this fact.

`ClientLevelModule.stopRenderer()` compare-and-sets the state reference to null
then closes its quadtree. Cache clearing keeps the same render-state identity
and calls `LodQuadTree.clearRenderDataCache()` under the tree lock. Terrain
updates queue section reloads. Identity polling therefore misses meaningful
within-state invalidation. Sampling on the render thread avoids some GL cleanup
races but does not freeze DH’s tree/source work. A positive certificate needs
explicit revision publication and invalidation before destructive mutation.

## Proposed diagnostic observer

A first implementation should publish only `UNKNOWN`, `INCOMPLETE` and
`NOMINAL_UPLOADED_FOOTPRINTS`, with missing cells and reasons. None authorize
automatic capping.

Use cached optional reflection handles with a strict artifact/version gate.
Prefer capturing primitive positions and container readiness while DH already
processes its enabled selection, avoiding another full scan. A pure polling
prototype can use private `enabledRenderSectionLock.tryLock()` with no wait,
a preallocated scratch buffer and a hard size limit; skip when contended or too
large. It must remain diagnostic because the lock does not freeze containers.
Do not call the public blocking list-copy method from a hot policy path, and do
not carry live list iterators across frames. Publish immutable primitive
snapshots; the Options getter reads only a cached decision and guards.

Suggested initial observer budget: run at most 4 Hz, at most 128 ring-intersecting
section records or 0.1 ms per step, ≤4,096 total records, ≤128 KiB primitive
snapshot storage and ≤16 KiB coverage bitmap storage per candidate region. These are proposed bounds to measure,
not verified costs. Cap lock-held inspection at a much smaller measured budget;
if snapshot publication cannot fit it, instrument publication rather than
extending the lock. Any overflow, contention, stale snapshot or budget exhaustion
returns `UNKNOWN`. Do not concatenate partial live snapshots into positive
coverage without a shared stable generation.

## Metadata needed for a positive certificate

A future adapter must associate each uploaded container with immutable source
coverage/revision metadata captured during DH’s existing conversion, not a new
storage read. Candidate hooks are the transformer return, section mesh-build
completion, successful container publication, and container close. Carry metadata
through source→builder→container identity; matching section position alone can
attach old metadata to a replacement upload. Treat missing association as unknown.

Publish a per-level selection generation and coverage epoch. Invalidate before
cache clear, reload/dirty marking, node deletion, container replacement/close,
world unload and renderer stop/config rebuild. Also track mesh-affecting DH
settings, shader pipeline, projection/camera mode, transparency and overdraw
settings. Stable immutable snapshots may then be processed across frames only
while epoch and identities remain unchanged. Independent worker callbacks need
well-defined release/acquire publication; the existing ordinary fields do not
provide that contract. This is explicit pinned integration, not arbitrary
reflection of another DH version.

## Ring and hierarchy algorithm after those blockers are solved

1. Define the terrain volume removed by the exact uncapped and capped Sodium
   section-selection rules. Start conservatively with an outer square enclosing
   every baseline selected chunk, including border chunks, and exclude only a
   verified guaranteed inner vanilla region. Do not certify only the forward
   camera frustum. Include DH/Photon overdraw and fade overlap. Photon v1.3b
   `dh_terrain.fsh` and `dh_water.fsh` start/end fading at
   `far - DH_OVERDRAW_DISTANCE - DH_OVERDRAW_FADE_LENGTH` and
   `far - DH_OVERDRAW_DISTANCE`; defaults are 16 blocks each. Establish the runtime
   `far` value and vanilla seam first; guessed cap×16 geometry is insufficient.
2. Expand the region for the true interpolated camera, third-person offset,
   candidate movement allowance and restoration latency. Use exact DH
   `RenderParams.exactCameraPosition` when appropriate; entity position alone
   does not describe all views. Initially limit activation to reviewed surface
   views; caves/underwater/culling rules require separate acceptance.
3. Decode each selected section via pinned `DhSectionPos` helpers into a half-open
   rectangle `[minX,minX+width) × [minZ,minZ+width)`, using checked long arithmetic.
   For raster cells use mathematical floor division, including negatives;
   `-0.1` and `-16.1` must not map to zero/−1 by truncation. Test axes, section
   boundaries and extreme world positions. Do not manually reinterpret packed
   coordinate bits.
4. Intersect those rectangles with the candidate ring. Only current selected,
   live uploaded containers with matching immutable metadata contribute coverage.
   An enabled coarse parent may cover its children if its complete-column
   metadata covers the entire queried area; DH’s `onDetailLevelTooLow` can retain
   a renderable parent and disable children until all four are ready. Do not
   require absent fine children when a certified parent covers them, and do not
   count disabled parent geometry simply because its container remains alive.
   For subdivision, coverage is parent-valid OR the union of certified selected
   children fully covering the query—not child count≥some threshold.
5. Conservatively reject partial cells. A fixed 16-block bitmap can represent
   nominal ring coverage only if every marked cell is entirely covered. When
   a source column is coarser or unknown, inspect its metadata-supported footprint
   explicitly. Reject incomplete source columns; known empty columns need a
   validated representation distinct from absent data. Opaque and transparent
   requirements differ: no water vertices alone does not prove water absent.
6. Include adjacent seam dependencies: the section builder loads four cardinal
   sources through `getRenderSourceForPos(..., direction)` and tests neighboring
   detail levels. Require valid neighbor provenance at coarse/fine boundaries,
   with a halo at least one relevant data-column width. Edge stitching quality
   and source completeness are separate checks. Expand or reject where the
   required neighbor lies outside the certified snapshot.
7. Publish a certificate containing region, allowed camera envelope, source,
   selection/upload epochs, world/pipeline identities and tested config signature.
   A ttl is only an additional guard; epoch invalidation is required. Any hole,
   stale/unknown state, unsupported setting or movement beyond the certified
   envelope restores the original request and revokes eligibility.

## Shadows, restoration and acceptance

A terrain-ring certificate does not preserve shadows automatically. The shadow
pass has its own frustum, while reducing the vanilla radius can remove detailed
casters, foliage, entities and block entities. Retain a detailed radius that
contains the verified shadow-caster region or separately prove DH shadow
coverage for the pinned Photon programs; comparing shadow-distance scalar to
cap alone does not prove projected caster coverage. Screen-space shadows and
reflection input also change when detailed geometry changes. This is a geometry
quality tradeoff even if shading budgets stay identical.

Uncapping an Options getter restores the *setting* immediately. Sodium then
needs time to rebuild/upload previously released detailed terrain. Safe travel
therefore needs a certified DH lookahead margin until detailed geometry has
actually recovered, or retained warm vanilla meshes. Teleports, high speeds and
cache clearing can invalidate that margin; fail-open policy is necessary but
cannot retroactively prevent a transient hole. Do not promise seamless arbitrary
travel from tick-time restoration alone or adjust radii every frame. Start with
fixed caps, activation dwell and verified steady scenes.

The first acceptance suite should exercise partial-column cold caches, coarse
parent fallback, all camera headings, negative-coordinate boundaries, source
updates during amortized scans, uploads failing/replacing/closing, independent
cache clear, renderer stop, dimension changes, third-person views, fast travel
and teleport restoration. Measure observer CPU/tail cost separately from gains;
inspect seam water/foliage/shadows and record actual selected/upload generations.
A positive automatic policy should remain off by default until those failures
restore safely and repeated motion tests pass. The immediate next deliverable
should be the bounded diagnostic observer, not automatic activation.

## Storage at preparation, run and finalization

Preflight checks 32 GiB plus the declared report/profile allowances on their
actual destination filesystems. Launch uses the existing serialized admission
with a 512 MiB profile-growth forecast, including the 96 GiB workload limit; the
canonical supervisor independently retains its normal admission. No APFS savings
or reduced reserve are assumed.

The operation checks filesystem free bytes and individual console/supervisor/game
log sizes during waits at most once per second. Full metadata checks cover only
its explicit report and selected profile, with a 100,000-entry ceiling. They occur
outside timing windows, never as a broad historical scan. Defaults are 256 MiB per
report, 512 MiB profile growth, 64 MiB per active log and 256 MiB total capture PNGs
in the scoped roots. Generated Iris source export must be Off. A reached limit
stops the attempt and preserves evidence; it never truncates an active log or
silently deletes captures. These are cooperative guard limits, not OS quotas:
one producer burst, the bounded sample interval for full checks, and unrelated
filesystem activity can exceed them. They do not reserve space against other
owners or bound the sum of historical report roots.

| Storage class | Producer and handling |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical scenes, shared packs/mods and other owners' profiles | Protected inputs; no caller deletion or copying into reports. |
| Resettable world-pool slots and world/DH data | Existing pool checkout/reset owns reuse; no hardlinks to writable worlds. Running growth has a declared cap. |
| Generated shader/export fanout | Source export disabled for this protocol; existing exports remain protected and counted. |
| Capture/raw timing evidence | Completed exports hashed and retained. `.storage-keep` pins raw evidence. Missing/invalid exports never pass completion. |
| Text logs | Size checked during waits; retained on success/failure for diagnosis. No active truncation. |
| Preparation/configuration backups | Exact manifested redundant copies retire only after verified terminal restore. Unknown backups remain protected. |
| Shared Gradle/dependency/build caches | Retained reusable inputs; no cache deletion or install by this change. |
| Unknown or historical artifacts | Inventory/preview only; an extension/category or age grants no disposal authority. |

Successful terminal restoration automatically journals and removes only the
operation's exact redundant configuration and supervisor-preparation backup
files. Every original path and backup hash is verified before deletion; unknown
files and pinned trees remain. For a recovered operation, explicitly request the
same narrow finalization with:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py recover --output dev/logs/my-authorized-run \
  --dispose-backups
```

Raw quality/capture evidence is never automatically retired by this caller. The
existing explicit `run_storage.py prune-captures` policy still requires no clients,
14-day age, `.storage-keep` exclusions, a journal and first/middle/last samples.
It marks retired raw motion evidence as incomplete. Historical maintenance stays
with its authorized owner, and is not run globally at experiment finalization.

Accounting distinguishes logical file length, per-file allocated blocks and
actual destination free bytes. Allocated blocks are not exclusive APFS bytes;
clones/snapshots can share them. WSL filesystem free space does not establish
Windows VHDX host-volume reclamation; that host backing is explicitly unmeasured.
Terminal backup-disposal receipts include before/after actual free bytes and a
concurrency caveat, not a claimed APFS reclaim amount.

## Footprint, work avoidance and fallback

The unchanged Photon normal evaluates **three**, not five, height samples at
`coord`, `coord+(0.1,0)` and `coord+(0,0.1)`. This revision retains those finite
differences, the original normal influence, flow classification, rain/skylight
and grazing suppression. It does not use the prior analytic-gradient approximation.

Full original normal evaluation remains selected through 32 Minecraft blocks.
A smoothstep from 32 to 48 blocks enables footprint filtering. Each octave's
carrier-plus-noise upper phase-frequency bound is evaluated using the actual
raster partials of its procedural coordinate. Squared sine has a second harmonic:
weights fade between 0.125 and 0.25 fundamental cycles per raster pixel (eight to
four pixels per fundamental cycle). The first octave always stays full; full-N
amplitude normalization remains unchanged. Footprint weights are computed once
and shared by the three height evaluations.

Zero-weight octaves skip noise lookup and trigonometry **before** that work.
Each omitted octave contributes its exact uniform-phase mean, 3/8, multiplied
by its original amplitude. Low-frequency height variation remains sampled and
multiplies the entire mean-containing field. This avoids amplifying the coarse
wave through reduced-N normalization or lowering mean height merely by dropping
amplitudes. Retained coarse height/slope amplitudes are preserved.

This is not a calibrated conditional noise mean or a guarantee of equivalent
normal variance/specular energy. High-frequency slope variance is intentionally
removed; no BRDF roughness compensation is applied. The modulation bound is an
upper bound, so it can conservatively overfilter actual resolved detail. Near
identity and phase mean do not establish distant sun-glint parity. The scalar
angle fixtures include an over-range flowing-water stress coefficient; corrected
source-domain results below still require matched runtime/motion review.

`WATER_PARALLAX=true` is supported. Before any discard, the first `main` block
initializes coordinates in all invocations, reproduces upstream corrected TBN and
flow setup, and evaluates full-quality parallax on water primitives when core
activation is valid. Glass does not run that height march. Returned coordinates
are reused at the original parallax site. After the material branch and adaptive
while have completed, unconditional `dFdx/dFdy` calls capture actual displaced
coordinates before the later material/normal LOD branch. Thus this does not guess
a world-distance ray cone or reuse the unwarped coordinate footprint.

[GLSL 4.10 section 3.8.2](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/GLSLangSpec.4.10.pdf)
says uniform control resumes after divergent substatements complete. Derivatives
at that reconverged point are raster approximations, not exact analytic Jacobians.
All operands are initialized, there is no discard or shader exit before capture,
and material/TBN inputs are flat within a primitive. Derivatives of the validity
flag execute in separate unconditional statements, avoiding short-circuit evaluation.

The full-height/parallax private clone preserves original arithmetic/loop counts
and only qualifies noise samples at explicit LOD0, plus invalid-path guards. Pinned
Photon custom `image/noise.png` is 512²; its mcmeta says blur=true/clamp=false.
Pinned Iris custom-PNG upload bytecode selects LINEAR min/mag and level-zero upload.
Reduced height uses explicit `textureGrad` with captured partials. These paths
introduce no implicit-gradient sample inside new dynamic control. Actual sampler
binding/mip state and driver sampling equivalence still require runtime readback;
upstream texture syntax alone does not prove undefined sampling with a no-mip
texture. Full near normal calls remain literal original; active full parallax is
mathematically preserved but no bit-identical GPU claim is made.

Zero initial height, singular/reversed tangent direction, singular interpolation,
nonfinite coordinates or excessive march count mark the private coordinate invalid.
The original downstream parallax/normal route remains the fallback, including
upstream behavior on those inputs; the private safety guards do not claim to fix
an upstream zero-height interpolation issue. A quad validity boundary also selects
full normal. Large parallax footprint amplification fades filtering out between
2× and 4× the unwarped footprint; at 4× full original normal is selected. This
protects unstable displaced-coordinate regions without a hard normal switch.

Private option off or other programs restore every upstream source byte after
resolving only new guards. Core absent/unknown or global off retains original
parallax and normal work. Enabled-source/global-off can retain small derivative/
control overhead; it is a distinct timing arm from pure original. Singular
persistence >=2.0 also falls back; Photon itself has singular full normalization
at persistence2.0, so this is baseline retention, not a mathematical repair.

# ShaderLOD benchmark upgrade plan

2026-10-25. Implementation plan for the official benchmark and tuning foundation.
Implementation and local acceptance are tracked in the [implementation report](evaluation/benchmark-upgrade-implementation-20261025.md).
This design document grants no runtime authority; the user request and managed STATUS own that.
Support and measured acceptance remain tuple-specific.
Sol drafted the architecture; Grok 4.7 reviewed it. The integrated review response
is [recorded here](evaluation/benchmark-upgrade-review-20261025.md).

## Purpose and priority

Make benchmarking a first-class development tool: find expensive **actual work**,
test why it costs time, and develop optimizations that save reproducible
milliseconds while preserving a stated visual contract. Automatic feature
selection is one consumer, not the benchmark's definition of success.

Use this development loop:

1. Profile the active render graph and locate costly CPU/GPU work.
2. State a hypothesis, removable-work headroom, expected total-frame benefit and
   still/motion quality boundary.
3. Implement one bounded change through the pinned family adapter.
4. Prove real consumption and reduced work, including added overhead.
5. Compare matched timing, quality and compatibility; optimize further, keep or
   park the result. Rank opportunities by credible milliseconds saved, uncertainty,
   effort and visual risk, rather than implemented feature count.

The [Mac diagnosis](evaluation/mac-dh-bottleneck-20261025.md) sets the immediate
priority. CPU2 reduced eligible command entries about 54.4%, but retained
34 world + 16 shadow GL submissions/frame. Same-pipeline observations at 1920 were
+10.7% FPS with DH disabled and +5.4% with DH enabled; roughly 1.6% at 2560 remained
within drift. Mean improvement did not guarantee p95 improvement. Master-Off
returned from 246 to 214 FPS. Neither suite gain nor PC causality is certified.
Repair control reliability before using the upgraded tool to promote changes.

Keep general shader performance in scope, with DH-heavy rendering a priority
workload. Focus research on measured expensive GPU work in shader-heavy cases,
while retaining useful CPU improvements and charging their costs explicitly.
The Mac data supports changing bottlenecks, not a universal GPU limit across
machines. Larger DH distances can add submission, streaming and memory costs
without proportional shaded-pixel growth; LOD opportunities require low visual
contribution as well as measured removable work. Hold user-selected distance,
native quality and AA fixed within benefit comparisons. Resolution/distance
ablations diagnose sensitivity; their quality changes are not suite gains.

## Existing foundation and proposed joins

Paths below describe current entry points; extend them rather than create another
independent timing harness.

| Existing component | Upgrade responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| [dev_client.py](../scripts/dev_client.py), especially `plan`, `supervise_locked`, `stop` | Canonical developer launch/boot, loaded-artifact verification, exclusive client ownership and finite deadline; default manual clients currently persist unless given `--stop-at`. |
| [BenchmarkScene](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/benchmark/BenchmarkScene.java), [BenchmarkWorld](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/benchmark/BenchmarkWorld.java), [BenchmarkStorage](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/benchmark/BenchmarkStorage.java) | Existing versioned authored Overworld, nine poses, route, construction/warming stages and ownership marker; add explicit scenario scheduling and readiness evidence. |
| [RuntimeMeasurement](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/measurement/RuntimeMeasurement.java), [FrameMeasurement](../src/benchmarkCore/java/com/pp/shaderlod/measurement/FrameMeasurement.java), [OpenGlElapsedBackend](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/measurement/OpenGlElapsedBackend.java) | Shared actual clocks, asynchronous bounded queries, epochs and opt-in recording; reconcile dev-runner scope definitions and observer modes. |
| [MeasurementPins](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/measurement/MeasurementPins.java), [MeasurementExport](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/measurement/MeasurementExport.java), [PairedMeasurement](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/measurement/PairedMeasurement.java) | Existing source/options pins, CSV export and finite return bracket; evolve one versioned result/analysis contract. |
| [AutoTuner](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/tuning/AutoTuner.java), [TuningWindow](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/tuning/TuningWindow.java), [TuningPolicy](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/tuning/TuningPolicy.java) | Existing screening, repeatability, final/motion stages and decisions; consume shared scenarios/statistics instead of owning a divergent protocol. |

The current documented benchmark/tuner target is Minecraft 1.21.1 NeoForge with
pinned Iris/Sodium. Other loaders/versions require explicit integration evidence.

## Canonical execution and ownership

Expose one scenario request/result contract to the menu benchmark, developer
runner and tuner. The launcher owns boot, process deadline and exact stop; the
mod owns world/scenario state and restoration; the shared measurement engine owns
clocks, validity, export and analysis. No second owner may mutate an active run.
Reuse one warmed client for compatible serial cases and feature trials; build
once per frozen revision and restart only when isolation or the changed stack
requires it. Client reuse must not disguise reload/history/cache transitions.
Keep shared scenario/measurement code usable by dev-only instrumentation when
the main mod is absent. Provision an equivalent canonical save before comparison;
the absent arm must not depend on the main-mod menu or inherit different route,
clock or observer semantics. This join is proposed, not existing absent-arm support
for the dedicated benchmark world.

Reuse stable loader/version/scene slots through
[run_storage.py](../scripts/run_storage.py) checkout. New world/profile copies use
`run_storage.copytree`; retain the 32 GiB free reserve, 96 GiB workload limit and
eight-slot bound. Keep canonical saves, reports and recovery evidence outside
disposable reset destinations; never share a writable live save. Runtime growth
needs bounded capture/export policies because launch admission alone cannot cap it.

Use the menu-owned save without disconnecting multiplayer or changing personal
worlds. Snapshot personal settings before mutation. Model the in-mod lifecycle as
prepare/open → construct-or-reuse → apply scenario → acknowledge → warm → measure
→ drain → evaluate → restore → verify/release. Every stage has a finite cutoff and
an explicit failed/incomplete outcome. Reserve recovery time separately from
sampling. Cancellation during synchronous driver calls completes when control
returns; the supervisor remains the outer deadline owner.

Restore source selection, requests, native quality/AA, video settings, camera,
time/weather and simulation state as applicable. Preserve original/Off/Quality,
Cancel, failed Apply and mismatched-source behavior. Failed restoration retains
the recovery owner/journal and blocks another run; release requires process exit,
save-lock release and verified restoration. Default gameplay adds no benchmark
overlay, polling, detailed profiling or export work; explicit runs use a small
progress/cancel display and a results link.

## Constant scene, scenarios and temporal semantics

Define a versioned **FAST** scenario: one constant dedicated authored scene and
short repeatable route, cycling terrain/foliage/cutouts, water/underwater,
materials/emissives/glass and distant terrain. Reuse the existing recipe and poses;
record which far geometry is actually visible at the selected RD. A material
panel does not establish active PBR/POM without the required resource pack/options.

Keep scene geometry and route constant between arms. Select named cases for
day/sunset/night, clear/rain/cold precipitation, RD, actual framebuffer resolution
and DH state. A case changes settings outside capture, acknowledges them, warms,
then measures; never mix changing geometry or environment into a steady-state
window. Route transitions may be a separately labeled streaming workload.

Warm-up must observe actual chunk meshing/lighting, DH loading/conversion queues,
draw/geometry stability, shader compilation/pipeline readiness and temporal
history convergence. Existing vanilla readiness and fixed dwell are insufficient
proof of DH settlement. Export observed readiness, missing signals, excluded
warm-up and timeout reasons. Choose bounded dwell/stability rules per scenario
and platform; impose no universal warm-up duration or stability threshold.
Settlement is also a capture validity rule: export queue and draw/index evidence
throughout the window, not only at entry. A drained queue with unexplained changing
geometry does not qualify a steady-state cell. Account for intended route/culling
changes using the scenario's work expectations. DH-On requires actual expected
distant terrain; PBR or effect-specific cases require their intended active work.
Missing coverage is unavailable or untested, not a cheap successful case.

Fixed camera/server time does not freeze shader animations, wetness smoothing,
frame counters or TAA histories. Default tests preserve native behavior and
record temporal inputs. A diagnostic replay must specify simulation time,
animation phase, frame counter/jitter sequence, partial ticks and history
reset/pre-roll semantics together. Freezing all clocks can disable or distort
temporal AA. Validate replay per pinned family; retain native-animation controls.
Match motion by route time/position and sampling coverage, not by rendered-frame
number alone. Report still and motion separately. Deliberately label cold boot,
cold pipeline/cache and warmed runs; never pool them as interchangeable repeats.

## Controls, clocks and result meaning

Maintain three explicit baselines:

- **ShaderLOD absent:** separate JVM, same original shader/options and equivalent
  scene, using dev-only observation without the main mod.
- **Installed masterOff:** native master switch path, including its lifecycle and
  source/reload behavior.
- **MasterOn/no requests:** installed enabled control for incremental features.

For runtime toggles that genuinely preserve the pipeline, compare no requests
versus feature and return, verifying source, effective options, pipeline identity
and reload count. Source-changing features, master transitions and reload tests
are distinct experiments with their own rewarming and counterbalanced returns.
Equal filenames/options do not establish pipeline equivalence. A win over an
artificially costly control is not original-relative benefit.

Export total frame intervals, render wall/thread CPU, process CPU with its exact
scope, and available GPU elapsed intervals. Describe omitted simulation,
presentation/limiter or timer routes. GPU elapsed is not hardware busy time;
CPU/GPU and nested scopes overlap and must not be summed. A missing DH_DRAW route
is missing coverage, not zero DH work. Report requested/valid/skipped/invalid
samples, timer resolution limits, query cadence and asynchronous tail handling.
Cross-check render-start intervals against whole-loop elapsed/frame counts;
instrumentation-free controls need an independent low-rate throughput observation,
not invented CPU/GPU measurements while their clocks are disabled.

Add low-rate heap occupancy/allocation and GC count/pause observations; label
native/process resident memory and GPU memory by API, availability and scope.
Unavailable or shared-memory estimates stay explicitly unavailable/qualified;
heap is not total process memory. Do not force GC during ordinary comparisons.
Keep settled-pose occupancy separate from labeled streaming-route growth and
peaks; record cache state and sampling cadence. Do not call an uncontrolled OS
cache cold or infer GPU residency from heap occupancy.
Collect actual work counters appropriate to the hypothesis: command entries,
GL submissions, DH draws/indices/queues, samples/pixels/pass invocations and
validation/cache hits. Separate requested, eligible and executed work.

Report mean frame milliseconds and throughput as reciprocal mean frame time,
not arithmetic mean instantaneous FPS; include median, p95/p99, stutters and
capture duration/counts. Tail latency is not uncertainty on a gain. Analyze
paired windows and independent JVM repeats with order/carryover noted; frames
are autocorrelated. Use counterbalanced returns, same-state controls and extra
repeats when they resolve a decision. Preserve negative, invalid, unavailable,
untested and inconclusive output; never select the best repeat. State uncertainty
and a case-specific practical benefit criterion without universal percentage gates.
Short-window p99 is descriptive and tagged with count/duration limitations; a
240-frame window has only a few observations in that tail. Tail inference needs
adequate paired windows or independent repeats and serial-dependence analysis;
several windows alone do not guarantee precision. Never use p99 as the sole gate.

Replace the live `TuningPolicy.stats/decide/repeatable/nonRegressing` promotion
logic with the shared analysis during milestone 2, including every trial,
confirmation, combined-profile and motion caller in `AutoTuner`. The current
implementation still uses independent-frame standard errors and fixed margins;
those live rules are not a new qualification standard. During migration, legacy
results remain explicitly legacy/unqualified by this protocol; there is no
legacy promotion fallback. Use paired-window effects and an explicit uncertainty
method that preserves serial dependence, with method, repeat count and assumptions
exported. Predeclare the practical benefit criterion and estimate repeatability
from the matching control class. Do not import a master-reload drift band into a
stable-pipeline experiment, or turn one observed drift into a universal threshold.

Before promotion, validate the instruments as well as the configuration baselines.
An unchanged-state/no-reload negative control must not become an optimization win;
a spurious win suspends promotion and triggers diagnosis, not retries until green.
A known-effect control names the clock/work signal expected to respond and its
preconditions: for example, calibrated CPU work or pacing, or resolution scaling
in an established graphics-sensitive case. Less GPU work need not improve total
time in a CPU-limited case. Synthetic controls are calibration only and cannot
serve as artificially slow optimization baselines. Save these controls and offline
null/known-effect sample fixtures to check the complete analysis/selection path.

Separate adaptive search from confirmation. Freeze a chosen combined profile,
then test a fresh return bracket and a predeclared held-out case/route segment
that candidate search cannot inspect. Report attempted candidates, retries and
search coverage. No saved winning profile depends solely on its search windows.
A failed holdout is reported and prevents promotion for that scope; further
development requires a new confirmation allocation, not repeated reuse of the
same holdout. State conditional workload wins and boundary regressions separately.

Calibrate observer cost using unchanged-state recording-off, coarse clocks,
sparse GPU queries and detailed profiling comparisons. Keep attribution windows
separate from low-overhead performance windows. Defer file writes, captures and
expensive source validation outside timed/render hot paths. Cache validation by
source/options/pipeline generation with explicit invalidation; retain a lightweight
safety guard until equivalent stale-source rejection is proved. No-op overhead
and altered query allocation/polling behavior require measured checks.
Charge the inverse tradeoff too: GPU work reduction can add CPU classification,
binding, submission, synchronization, extra passes or bandwidth. Report net total
frame and CPU costs per supported tuple. Backends expose capability/coverage and
clock validity; reset, disjoint or invalid results are rejected where the API can
detect them, never filled with zero. Do not assume a portable GPU-busy counter or
the same timer/disjoint APIs on Windows and Apple OpenGL.

## Shared result contract

Milestone 2 implements one versioned manifest/window/sample/decision contract,
used by both the developer runner and tuner. Minimum fields are:

- Run/comparison/window IDs, schema and analysis versions; scenario/route revision,
  tuple and loaded-artifact identities, device/OS/driver/JVM, selected source,
  effective options/resources/AA, viewport, distances, DH and cache state.
- Arm (`absent`, `masterOff`, `masterOn-no-requests`, feature, return), feature
  profile, source/pipeline generations, reload count, order, cold/warm and
  search/holdout labels, temporal inputs, warm-up and host observations.
- Clock names/units/boundaries/domains, omitted routes, backend capabilities,
  query cadence/epochs/tail handling; raw frame IDs and requested, valid, skipped
  and invalid counts with reasons. Preserve unavailable values as unavailable.
- Requested, eligible and executed work; hypothesis-specific units such as
  command entries, submissions, samples, bytes or pass invocations, plus queue
  and geometry evidence. No single counter type is mandatory for every mechanism.
- Mean frame ms and reciprocal-mean throughput, median/p95/p99 and their sample
  limitations, stutter definition/count, window/JVM repeat counts, order/carryover,
  uncertainty method, paired effects and predeclared decision criterion.
- Separate availability, activation, measurement validity and effect verdict.
  A valid negative result differs from invalid measurement, unavailable feature,
  untested coverage and inconclusive effect; each has a reason and recovery status.
- Still/motion evidence links, quality/compatibility verdicts, observer mode/cost,
  restoration journal/status and final ownership release.

Do not pool heterogeneous scenarios, devices or cold/warm states into a headline.
Publish per-case effects and coverage first; any aggregate declares its weights,
method and worst regressions. Missing required fields prevent the relevant claim.

## Staged coverage and milestones

Use three tiers, not a Cartesian product. **Fast iteration** runs FAST with one
representative active workload and local controls. **Diagnostic** expands only
the suspected bottleneck using sparse profiles, resolution/RD changes or DH
isolation. **Matrix qualification** follows a promising result across selected
families, hardware and loader/version tuples. Preserve native quality/AA and
licenses/ancestry. Compatibility has a separate verdict: DH absent,
installed-disabled and enabled; PBR resource/options; AA modes; dimensions and
family/loader/version boundaries. Compatibility success alone is no performance win.
Select representative CPU/submission-sensitive, shader/pixel-sensitive and
DH-heavy cases rather than assuming one pose exposes every optimization. A GPU
candidate starts with an active graphics-sensitive workload; the lighter case
remains a CPU-overhead/regression check. This is targeted coverage, not all
combinations of every setting.

1. **Control reliability first.** Reproduce/diagnose master-return drift with
   same-state/no-reload, same-configuration reload and the three baselines;
   distinguish temporal phase, queue/geometry, observer and host-state hypotheses.
   Check default benchmark inactivity, recording/query overhead and timer-route
   coverage. Accept when repeated matched controls bound detectable benefit for
   the chosen case and restoration succeeds; otherwise emit inconclusive and
   retain the diagnosis. No optimization promotion depends on an unresolved control.
   Include negative/known-effect instrument checks and explicit work eligibility.
2. **Shared engine and recovery, after initial control diagnosis.** Join runner/tuner requests to common
   clocks, epochs, schema and analysis. Check stale/missing samples, delayed query
   tails, cancellation, reload/fallback, source mismatch and interrupted recovery;
   identical saved samples must yield identical statistics and validity decisions
   in both consumers. Replace all live legacy promotion callers; test null-search
   behavior and fresh holdout confirmation. Resolve neutral-core packaging so the
   absent arm can use the same schema/analysis without loading the main mod.
   Verify owned boot/stop and storage reuse end to end.
   If missing shared/absent observation blocks a control in milestone 1, implement
   this minimal join first, then finish that control; never substitute a different
   clock or require every control to pass before repairing its own instruments.
3. **FAST scenarios, after 2.** Version route/environment schedules and readiness
   providers. Check deterministic reconstruction, repeated case/route alignment,
   cold/warm labels, DH queue timeouts and temporal replay/native-AA semantics.
   Show actual scenery/material coverage and unobtrusive normal gameplay.
4. **Optimization development, after 1–3.** Profile one expensive active path;
   consider DH render/integration alongside general shader work. Require a
   headroom hypothesis, consuming-work reduction, matched total-frame/tail result
   and still/motion inspection. Keep or park with reasons; CPU savings alone do
   not establish throughput gain.
   Require a matched-camera still pair and a short motion/temporal assessment for
   the changed effect before performance promotion. A GPU-only metric is likewise
   insufficient; exact-output CPU mechanisms may instead reuse current applicable
   quality evidence with an explicit reference.
   Compare against baseline-to-baseline temporal variation; inspect shimmer,
   ghosting/disocclusion and transitions rather than treating static pixel-error
   scores as perceptual certification.
5. **Qualification and tuner adoption, after 4.** Expand representative cases to
   expose bottleneck/quality boundaries, then targeted interactions and supported
   tuples. Require separate compatibility receipts and independent confirmation
   of promising timings. Let the tuner consume qualified measurement semantics;
   finite search coverage and a saved profile never certify universal image quality.

Use [Evaluation](EVALUATION.md), [Repeated benchmarks](REPEATED_BENCHMARKS.md),
[measurement reliability](GENERAL_LOD_MEASUREMENT_RELIABILITY.md),
[tuning](BENCHMARK_TUNING.md), [storage](BENCHMARK_STORAGE.md) and
[operations](AGENT_OPERATIONS.md) as implementation constraints. Historical fixed
thresholds and old runs remain historical evidence, not universal new gates.

## First delivery slice and provisional budgets

Start milestone 1 on the Mac's pinned MC1.21.1 NeoForge/Iris/Sodium tuple, MakeUp,
the existing coast pose, RD12 and actual1920×1200. Diagnose same-state no-reload,
same-configuration reload and the three baselines in separate control classes.
Add settled DH-disabled/enabled cells only when they answer the next uncertainty;
BSL is the second family check. This reuses inputs rather than opening a new matrix.
Record a case-specific benefit/detection target before timing; revise it only in
a new stated experiment if control noise makes the original target unresolved.

The warm-client FAST target is at most three minutes for one focused comparison,
including transition/warm-up/capture/export. This is a proposed usability target,
not measured current throughput or permission to weaken evidence. Boot/world
preparation is reported separately alongside end-to-end time. Bound a diagnostic
batch to fifteen minutes including recovery; separate-JVM baselines may need
several named batches. Budget exhaustion reports partial/inconclusive coverage.
The initial slice need not solve universal replay, memory APIs or every family.

Milestone 1 first delivers saved control records, instrument-calibration evidence,
explicit unresolved causes and a justified next action. Milestone 2 delivers the
shared schema/analyzer and tuner-call migration; milestone 3 wires the dedicated
authored FAST route to that engine. These are executable increments, not one large
benchmark rewrite.

## Decisions to settle during integration

- Validate or revise the provisional FAST budget and representative case after
  the first control study; do not promise detectability before controls establish it.
- Choose which pinned family can support honest temporal replay; otherwise ship
  native-animation repeatability first and label replay unavailable.
- Choose shared schema/analysis placement and supported memory/queue providers;
  missing platform APIs must not delay honest partial reporting.
- Select the first qualification tuples and visual reviewer. PC execution remains
  paused unless separately assigned; this plan makes no PC bottleneck claim.

# Shadow-only visibility traversal reuse design

Source-only design, 2026-10-04. No implementation, builds, games or benchmarks
were performed for this document. Inputs are pinned Sodium 0.6.13 commit
`8672650501117e72f5a809867092378fb5bc908a` and the exact Iris 1.8.12 NeoForge
artifact described in `VISIBILITY_REUSE_AUDIT.md`. Its ignored source and verbose
bytecode review paths are the source authority for the line/offset references
below. The default-off inner-list prerequisite compiled and passed model tests;
that is neither a performance gain nor proof this cache is safe.

## Bounded opportunity and recommendation

Cache **only the shadow graph search/list construction** when a complete
structural epoch and exact traversal inputs are unchanged. Main traversal
continues normally. Preserve Iris's forced dirty mark, manager update's frame
increment and Iris's cancellation after list construction; do not clear the
shared dirty flag or cancel terrain setup at HEAD.

This could avoid repeated exact work while a camera, sun and graph remain
unchanged, but exact input equality probably misses on most normal moving-sun
frames. A daylight-frozen benchmark can test mechanism correctness; it cannot
establish useful gameplay acceptance. A conservative frustum envelope is a
possible later policy with extra draw cost, requiring a real bound rather
than approximate matrix equality. Neither implementation is approved by this
source-only design.

## Side effects the cache must reproduce

`RenderSectionManager.update` increments `lastUpdatedFrame`, calls
`createTerrainRenderList(camera,viewport,frame,spectator)`, then normally clears
its dirty flag (`RenderSectionManager.java:131–136`). Iris cancels shadow update
after that call, before the clear. Keeping the call boundary means the cache
can replace/replay its body while the original frame increment and Iris
after-call behavior remain. A boolean head-cancel of update would change them.

The original construction does more than return a draw-list pointer:

| State | Producer | Consumers/replay obligation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shadow outer render list | Collector creation and manager field write | Terrain draw/list counts need the same ordered per-region membership |
| Owner-local inner lists | Region getter, reset/add/sort | Independent shadow arrays must retain the exact section IDs/order/counts |
| Shadow task maps/queues | Reset plus collector `getRebuildLists()` | Queues cannot retain stale pending/cancelled jobs or lose new jobs |
| Manager traversal stamp | Update increments before construction | Continue original increment; do not confuse cached stamp with game frame |
| Region-list visible stamp | Collector resets owner list with current traversal stamp | Retag cached shadow list for current generation without clearing membership |
| Section visible stamp | Culler enqueue/nearby/origin operations | Replay every touched section, including non-rendering sections |
| Section incoming directions | Culler initializes then unions graph paths | Replay recorded final direction bits; don't overwrite unrelated main state |
| Region sort/order | Collector + local sorting | Exact key includes camera section/region origin; translucent order remains unchanged |
| Sprite activation | `tickVisibleRenders` main-container entries | Existing generation-aware sprite adapter must see current shadow provenance |

The important distinction is **touched versus rendered**. In
`OcclusionCuller.java:156–166`, enqueue stamps a section and updates incoming
directions before `processQueue` later rejects it for distance/frustum. Empty
sections also participate in traversal/task scheduling. Nearby-section and
origin paths stamp separately (lines 250–254 and 291–307). Therefore retaining
only `VisibleChunkCollector.visit` objects or geometry arrays is insufficient.

`RenderSectionManager.isSectionVisible` compares a section stamp against the
current manager stamp (lines 282–292). Sodium's entity visibility path calls
it (`SodiumWorldRenderer.java:479–526`). Even if a particular shadow scene has
no entities, those side effects cannot be omitted as "unused." Main traversal
will subsequently overwrite the same shared section graph metadata normally.

On an exact cache hit, replay the captured touched-section set's stamps and
final direction unions, refresh each cached region-list generation, and restore
the shadow outer container/empty task maps for the current invocation. This is
an O(touched sections) operation, not free constant-time reuse. It can still
avoid repeated plane/distance tests, graph connectivity expansion, allocations
and sorting. Compare replay cost to those avoided operations before claiming
whole-frame benefit.

New inner-list retagging needs an explicit method that changes only its private
generation field. Calling `reset(frame)` would erase membership. No such retag
API was added by the no-skip prerequisite. Unknown/provenance-incomplete data
always falls back to original traversal.

## Genuine producer epochs

One shared boolean is not a freshness certificate. A cache needs a monotonic
structural generation bound to a particular manager/world and a separate
pending-task generation. Instrument all actual writers first:

| Hook/reason | Actual source behavior | Required invalidation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manager constructor, renderer `initRenderer`, unload/reload | New manager/region/section identities; starts dirty | Drop the entire cache, never copy snapshots between managers/worlds |
| `onSectionAdded` success | New node/neighbor connections and pending initial build; direct dirty true | Structural and task epochs; duplicate no-op adds need not falsely certify freshness |
| `onSectionRemoved` success | Disconnects/removes/deletes section and sort data; direct dirty true | Structural/task epochs and disposed-reference invalidation |
| `scheduleRebuild` promotion | New pending type, cache invalidation, direct dirty true | Task epoch immediately; structural epoch conservatively until successful build is observed |
| `uploadChunks/processChunkBuildResults` | Uploads before conditional OR of graph-changing info | Structural epoch for built/flag/connectivity/global-entity changes; preserve all uploads regardless of cache |
| Sort scheduling/promotion | `scheduleSort` changes pending state without necessarily marking graph dirty | Pending-task/sort epoch; cached queues cannot infer safety from clean graph alone |
| Task cancellation/retirement | Tokens, pending types, submit/upload stamps change | Task epoch; no stale queue/token reuse |
| Public `markGraphDirty` / external terrain-update request | Broad caller-provided invalidation | Conservatively invalidate unless the exact redundant shadow-force call is identified |
| Camera/frustum/search/mode change | Ordinary setup marks dirty and updates sorting/camera state | Exact phase input key; these operations still run outside cache replacement |
| Pipeline/pack/resources/vertex-format change | Replaces renderer/frustum/program settings | Pipeline generation and manager identity; force complete miss |

The repeated Iris shadow force is a **reason**, not structural world change:
`ShadowRenderer.renderShadows` bytecode 399 → Sodium LevelRendererMixin
`needsUpdate` RETURN → `scheduleTerrainUpdate` → `markGraphDirty`. Classify only
that exact call boundary, with a nonallocating render-thread scope if later
implemented. Unknown marks remain conservative misses. Do not suppress the
mark itself: preserving main rebuild is part of this bounded design.

Direct field writes and `needsGraphUpdate |= processChunkBuildResults` must be
covered, not merely public `markGraphDirty`. Uploads with unchanged mesh-info
can change GPU storage/translucent data even when they do not need a visibility
rebuild; preserving normal draw/storage APIs matters. Cache only membership,
never baked native draw pointers or index-arena offsets.

A conservative first exact cache should refuse a hit whenever any relevant
pending build/sort/cancellation queue or job is present, or its task epoch
changed. This avoids trying to reuse/recollect mutable shadow task queues in
the first prototype. It reduces hit rate during loading/editing and must be
reported as a restriction, not hidden by waiting only for a static benchmark.

## Exact key and expiry

Required key fields include manager and world identity, pipeline/resource
generation, current supported Photon/runtime identity, shadow culling class
(advanced/reversed/box/nonculling), exact prepared plane coefficients/count,
distance-box parameters, camera origin/position/rotation, viewport camera
transform and section origin, search distance, effective occlusion/spectator
mode, shadow range/projection settings and DH projection/readiness selection.
The key is per shadow terrain traversal, not a global "same camera" flag.

Actual plane comparison may be a better validity key than comparing only an
input projection matrix, because it directly represents the test performed.
Compare every value exactly; any incomplete/non-finite/unknown input misses.
Hashing alone is insufficient: compare stored values after a hash match.
Use original conversion/rounding semantics for relative float endpoints.

`ShadowRenderer.createShadowFrustum` constructs light direction from celestial
uniforms, normalizes it, selects captured vanilla or DH projection, multiplies
by captured model view and generates advanced/reversed planes. Its bytecode
at 423–580 records these dependencies. `AdvancedShadowCullingFrustum` chooses
back/edge planes according to light/plane relationships; edge construction
includes cross products and division by squared edge length. Quantizing the
sun angle or matrix can change included casters near boundaries.

Normal daylight interpolates continuously. Exact celestial direction and
generated coefficients will commonly change even with a stationary player.
Camera motion, bobbing/FOV/projection changes and DH projection updates cause
additional misses. Measure actual hit-rate in real time before engineering
for only frozen-clock captures. Unknown metadata cannot be declared stable by
an elapsed warmup or a heuristic epsilon.

## Later choice: conservative frustum envelope

A safe envelope must contain the **union** of caster acceptance sets over a
declared bounded camera/light interval. It can include extra sections; it may
never omit a current accepted section. Approximate equality of two frusta does
not provide that property.

One mathematically bounded construction uses stable baseline halfspaces. For
a baseline plane `L0(x)=n0·x+d0`, bound every corresponding current plane over
the interval by `||n(t)-n0|| <= eta`, `|d(t)-d0| <= beta`, and bound relevant
camera-relative points by `||x|| <= R`. Also account for camera translation
`delta` and outward-rounded floating-point evaluation error `epsilon`.
Relax the cached plane by a margin at least

`R*eta + max(||n(t)||)*delta + beta + epsilon`.

If a current point satisfies its plane, its baseline expression is no smaller
than the negative of this margin. The relaxed baseline plane therefore contains
it. With valid corresponding constraints, intersecting these relaxed halfspaces
gives a conservative envelope. Box/section acceptance uses the padded AABBs,
including Sodium's 9.125f section extent; the error bound must cover corners
and exact float evaluation, not just section centers.

Important conditions make this a design rather than a ready formula:

- A cached plane needs a valid corresponding constraint throughout the interval.
  If light/back-plane classification or edge topology can remove it, drop that
  constraint from the envelope or force a rebuild. Endpoint sampling alone
  cannot bound the nonlinear cross-product/division path.
- Prove coefficient intervals and finite domain `R` from actual bounded
  camera, light, projection and distance-box inputs. Near-degenerate edge
  denominators or unknown/non-finite values require a miss or a broader safe
  fallback, not an arbitrary epsilon.
- The cached distance/search domain must include the union of current camera
  distance tests. A camera-cell-expanded box/cylinder supplies a simple bound;
  use the same strict/inclusive source comparisons with outward margins.
- Traversal pruning must be compatible with the envelope. For the ordinary
  shadow path, `ShadowRenderer` temporarily disables `smartCull`; confirm the
  effective flag from the actual call. If occlusion is enabled, camera-dependent
  angle masks/origin outward directions can change reachability. A superset
  plane volume alone does not prove a superset graph walk. Restrict that variant
  or build a conservative unoccluded candidate universe explicitly.

A trivially conservative fallback is all available sections within the union
of shadow distance/search bounds, ignoring advanced clipping. That is useful
as a correctness oracle, but may add many geometry draws/native submissions.
It is not an attractive optimization by assumption. A tighter bounded envelope
can amortize graph search over tiny movement/sun intervals, but its additional
caster/section count, draw calls and GPU cost must be measured separately from
CPU traversal savings. Shadow-map extra content and translucent/colored
shadow ordering still require visual validation.

This policy preserves all current casters while accepting extra work; it is
distinct from reducing vanilla radius or dropping distant shadows. A reduced
geometry/detail radius changes quality/reach and remains a separate existing
knob. No fixed angular envelope or tolerance is recommended before bound and
cost evidence.

## Lifecycle and acceptance matrix

| Case | Required behavior / evidence |
| --- | --- |
| First eligible frame or unknown key | Full traversal, capture complete touched/list/task provenance |
| Exact unchanged key, empty task epochs | Replay all side effects; same ordered memberships/caster set and current stamps |
| Sun moves with player still | Exact cache misses unless a separately proven envelope contains current frustum |
| Camera rotates/translates/FOV changes | Miss or proven envelope coverage; preserve nearby/origin traversal behavior |
| New/removed/replaced region/section | Immediate epoch invalidation; no dereference of disposed owners |
| Block edit and async build upload | Current task scheduling/storage upload continues; refreshed memberships when flags/connectivity change |
| Pending sort/token completion | Miss/recollect under first conservative design; no lost/stale jobs |
| Main traversal after reused shadow | Forced dirty remains true; ordinary main rebuild and current entity visibility still work |
| Animated surfaces/shadow casters | Sprite adapter observes replayed current region stamps; compare actual activation identity sets |
| World/dimension/manager/shader reload | Cache fully dropped, no cross-identity snapshots |
| Feature toggled/global disabled/fallback | Original traversal immediately; safe repopulation and default-off behavior |
| Optional DH enters/leaves/projection changes | Miss unless exact selected input remains proven unchanged; DH's own terrain lifecycle untouched |
| Integer generation wrap/long runs | Same upstream equality semantics with epoch wrap protected; no accidental ancient hits |
| Reversed/colored-light or other frustum class | Unsupported until separate proof; fall back to original behavior |

Start with no-skip reason counters and immutable diagnostic snapshots. Then
prove exact-cache output against an always-traverse oracle on every lifecycle
case, including enqueued-but-rejected and empty sections. Inspect actual sprite,
entity/task progress and movement images. A second diagnostic can compare a
conservative envelope's candidates against current original acceptance and
assert set containment each frame without changing rendered results.

Only after correctness, measure repeated serial main/shadow traversal CPU,
replay CPU, total frame/GPU/native draw cost and real-play hit/miss reasons.
Include walking/turning/daylight, loading/edits, DH and optimizer-stack controls.
A frozen-world-age/fixed-camera improvement alone fails this acceptance.
The Photon ordinary performance gate and second shader expansion remain
independent requirements. There is no safe traversal skip implemented here.

members; `cost_map_features.py` contains the mixed feature labels. Runtime binding
requires that archive, Overworld, the owned selected/preprocessed graph and its
actual effective options. A filename/family guess cannot activate tags. Unknown
archives/dimensions remain unmapped. Labels describe potential features in a mixed
program, including conditional code; they do not time individual shader functions.

| Family / originals | Dedicated world raster joins | Shared DH consumers reviewed in original source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reimagined r5.9.3 and Unbound r5.9.3 | `dh/world/opaque` → `dh_terrain`; translucent → `dh_water` | deferred1 LOD depth/shadow/AO/atmosphere; composite1 volumetric light/water fog; composite3 depth/fog; composite4/5 depth-aware post; TAA helpers consume DH depth |
